gaps.name: compute-runner-interface
gaps.title: A runner interface in the core, its first backend today's local runs
gaps.definition:
Problem. A machine block's run reaches its process directly in five places, so nothing but this machine can execute one (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 1, milestone gap 1). `Engine._ran` starts it inline (ergostat/spec/engine.py:1060-1110: runrecord.files, Measured, runrecord.write, old.LIVE, self.procs, self.live, SAMPLER.track, reap.Watch, stream.follow, runrecord.remove, SAMPLER.finish); `stop_run` kills `self.procs[name]` (engine.py:1855-1865); `close` calls `old.kill_all` or kills `self.live` (engine.py:1985-2001); the lease kill looks the run up in `eng.live` and reads `proc.watch` (ergostat/leases/kill.py:39-62); `runner.LIVE`/`kill_all` hold every run (ergostat/runner.py:38-59).

Change. New `ergostat/compute/__init__.py` and `ergostat/compute/runner.py`: a `Runner` protocol with `start(spec) -> Handle`, `follow(handle, take, timeout, offset=0) -> bool` (timed out; the offset taken kept on the handle), `alive(handle)`, `kill(handle, why, grace) -> bool`, `resources(handle) -> dict | None`, `cleanup(handle)`, and `local`, a backend that is today's code moved behind it unchanged (the wrapper and run files, Measured, the sampler, stream.follow, reap.Watch, registration in runner.LIVE). `_ran`, `stop_run`, `close` and `leases/kill.py` reach runs only through handles (`self.live` maps run id to a Handle; `kill.py` calls the handle's stop with the grace, recording `ergostat.run.killed` exactly as now). `runner(spec, block)` returns the backend for a block: always `local` in this gap. Daemon runs (engine.py:1046-1051) stay as they are. No behaviour changes.

Definition of done.
1. `ergostat/compute/runner.py` defines the protocol and the `local` backend; `_ran` holds no `Measured`, `runrecord` or `stream` call of its own.
2. `stop_run`, `close` and `leases/kill.py` reach a run through its handle; `eng.live` holds handles.
3. The records a run writes (agent.started, agent.ran/failed with exit, note, resources; ergostat.run.killed with signal and pids) keep exactly the same shape as before.
4. The unit suite and the four browser files pass unchanged; no test is edited except imports.
5. SPEC §9.1 names the interface in one paragraph.

Files: ergostat/compute/__init__.py (new), ergostat/compute/runner.py (new), ergostat/spec/engine.py, ergostat/leases/kill.py, ergostat/runner.py (only if LIVE registration moves), tests/test_compute_runner.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

- ::test_lease_kill_goes_through_the_handle: an expired lease's kill calls the backend's kill with the grace and records ergostat.run.killed with the same fields tests/test_lease_kill.py expects.
- ::test_stop_run_and_close_kill_through_handles.
- tests/test_lease_kill.py, tests/test_streamed_output.py, tests/test_sampler_ramp.py pass unchanged.

gaps.name: compute-run-spec
gaps.title: A run as one JSON-able spec handed to its runner
gaps.definition:
Problem. What a run is (command, input, cwd, environment, limits) is spread over local variables of `_ran` (ergostat/spec/engine.py:1002-1059): `cmd, stdin = self.program(...)` (engine.py:1002, 1041), `env = {**os.environ, ...}` (engine.py:995-1027), `cwd` (engine.py:1046), `b.timeout`. A backend on another machine can take none of it, and the engine's whole environment (every secret it was started with) is in each run's (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md sections 1 and 2.6, milestone gap 2).

Change. `ergostat/compute/spec.py`: a `RunSpec` dataclass with `to_json()`/`from_json()`: run id, block, block type, command, input, cwd, `env` (only the `ERGOSTAT_*` variables `_ran` sets today), `secrets` (names only), `limits` (`wall` from the block's timeout; cpus, memory, pids, disk, network, log: None unless given), `work` (repo name and commit, None by default), `out` (bundle, artifacts, transcripts; empty by default), `lease` (fence, ttl, expires). `_ran` builds one and passes it to `runner.start`. The `local` backend still runs with `{**os.environ, **spec.env}` (today's behaviour, said in a comment); `RunSpec.allowlisted_env()` returns `PATH`, `HOME`, `LANG`, the `ERGOSTAT_*` variables and the secrets named, which later backends use. Run ids are checked against `^[0-9a-f]{32}$` for any backend but local.

Definition of done.
1. `_ran` builds exactly one RunSpec per run and hands it to the runner; the local backend's process sees the same environment, input, cwd and command as before.
2. A RunSpec round-trips through JSON unchanged for every machine block type that runs a process (program and ai; a leased run, an event-started run, a commanded run).
3. `allowlisted_env()` never contains a variable of the engine's own environment beyond PATH, HOME and LANG.
4. No secret value is a field of RunSpec (names only).

Files: ergostat/compute/spec.py (new), ergostat/compute/runner.py, ergostat/spec/engine.py, tests/test_compute_spec.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

Acceptance tests.
- tests/test_compute_spec.py::test_spec_of_each_block_type_round_trips.
- ::test_local_run_environment_unchanged: a program block printing `env` sees the same variables before and after (an engine variable set in the test included).
- ::test_allowlist_holds_no_engine_variable: an `ENGINE_ONLY=x` in os.environ is absent from `allowlisted_env()`.
- ::test_leased_spec_carries_fence_ttl_expires.

gaps.name: compute-pools-config
gaps.title: compute: and runs-on: in the model, with their check findings and ceilings
gaps.definition:
Problem. A model cannot say where a block's runs execute: there is no `compute:` section and no `runs-on:` key (machine keys are ergostat/spec/compile.py:86-92; top-level sections such as `workspaces:` are compiled by their own module, ergostat/workspaces/compile.py:15-41, called at compile.py:1066-1068). The proposal's model (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 4) and ceilings (sections 2.7, 3) need a home and a `check`.

Change. `ergostat/compute/compile.py`, called from the spec compiler beside `workspaces`: `compute:` pools (`nodes: [{ssh: HOST} | {connect: [argv]}]`, `backend: process|docker`, `image`, `slots`, `limits: {cpus, memory, pids, disk, wall, network, log}` with sizes like `4g` and durations like `30m`, `repos: {name: path}`, `secrets: {NAME: file}`, `labels`) into a `ComputePool` in the IR (ergostat/spec/ir.py beside `WorkspacePool`, ir.py:503); `runs-on: POOL|local` on machine blocks into `Block.runs_on` (ir.py:695-725, default None = local). Errors, each with where it was written: unknown pool; unknown key; a bad size or duration; nodes over 64; slots over 64; the sum over pools of nodes x slots over 256; wall over a day; log over 1 GiB; `network: none` on the process backend; `docker` without `image`; a `runs-on` block that is a daemon, a sensor, an `ai` block (later), or whose command names `ERGOSTAT_CMD`, `ERGOSTAT_SOCKET` or `ergostat ` (calls from a node are a later gap); a pool used by blocks of two shards (SPEC §9.8, dispatch.py:96-100); a node entry naming an address or a user (`@` in `ssh:`; a host must be a name in the owner's ssh config). Nothing runs differently yet: the engine ignores `runs_on` until compute-remote-backend.

Definition of done.
1. A model with `compute:` and `runs-on:` compiles; the IR holds the pools and each block's `runs_on`.
2. Each refusal above is an error with its code and place.
3. A model without `compute:` compiles to an identical IR (no new fields set).
4. SPEC gains a `compute:` subsection in the model reference (section 4 of the proposal, trimmed), and `runs-on` in the machine block keys.

gaps.name: compute-worker-protocol
gaps.title: ergostat worker --stdio: the protocol's frame, hello, beat and ping
gaps.definition:
Problem. Nothing on another machine can speak to the engine: there is no `ergostat worker` (ergostat/cli/__init__.py:356-369 lists every topic) and no protocol (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md sections 2, 2.1, 3; milestone gap 3, split here: this gap is the frame and registration only).

Change. `ergostat/compute/worker.py`, standard library only and with no package-relative imports, so `python3 -I worker.py --stdio` runs it with no ergostat installed; `ergostat worker --stdio [--root DIR]` (new `ergostat/cli/worker.py`, registered in cli/__init__.py) calls the same `main`. It reads one JSON object a line on stdin and writes one a line on stdout, diagnostics to stderr. Every line has `v` (1), `seq` (per direction from 1) and `type`, at most 1 MiB (a longer one answered `error` and the session ended); requests carry `id`, answers repeat it. First line `hello`: `node` (a random 32-hex id made once and kept in the root, never a host name, address or user), `cpus`, `memory`, `disk.root`, `arch`, `os`, `backends` (['process']), `images` ([]), `labels` (from `labels.json` in the root), `slots` (its config `slots.json`, at most its CPUs, at most 64), `runs` ([] until compute-worker-restart-states). `beat` every 10 s with slots free and disk free; `ping` answered `pong` at once; a line of another `v` answered `error` then exit; an unknown `type` answered `error` without ending. The root defaults to `~/.local/state/ergostat-worker/` and the worker writes nowhere else. A tiny test helper `tests/compute_pipe.py` starts the worker over a pipe and reads its lines.

Definition of done.
1. `python3 -I ergostat/compute/worker.py --stdio --root R` and `ergostat worker --stdio --root R` both answer `hello` then `pong` to a `ping`.
2. The node id persists across restarts and matches `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`.
3. `seq` increases by one on every line out; a gap in the engine's seq is said on stderr.
4. An over-long line, a wrong `v` and an unknown type are each answered as above.
5. Nothing is written outside the root (a test lists the filesystem diff under a temporary HOME).
6. SPEC gains a short *Compute systems* section naming the worker and protocol v1.

Files: ergostat/compute/worker.py (new), ergostat/cli/worker.py (new), ergostat/cli/__init__.py, tests/compute_pipe.py (new), tests/test_compute_worker_protocol.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

gaps.name: compute-worker-keeper
gaps.title: The worker starts a run under its keeper, which holds its deadlines
gaps.definition:
Problem. A run started by an SSH-launched worker would die with the session or outlive every deadline: a local run's wrapper only writes the exit (ergostat/spec/runrecord.py:22-30) and holds no timeout (the timeout lives in the engine's follower, ergostat/spec/stream.py:36-38). The proposal puts the deadlines in a detached per-run keeper (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md sections 2.2 process backend, 2.4, 2.7 wall timeout; milestone gap 3).

Change. In ergostat/compute/worker.py: `start` (run id checked `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`, else `refused bad name`; `full` past slots; `limits over the node`) makes `runs/RUN/` in the root with `run.json` (run id, block, lease fence, backend, limits, wall deadline, keeper pid and start time), `in`, an empty folder as cwd, the first `deadline` file, then starts the keeper `python3 -I worker.py --keep RUN --root R` detached (setsid, stdin /dev/null, output to runs/RUN/keeper.log, SIGHUP ignored) and answers `started` with the pid and its start time, or `refused no keeper`. The keeper forks the run: own process group, `pgid` file written before exec, setrlimit RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_NPROC (and RLIMIT_CPU at cpus x wall), on Linux PR_SET_PDEATHSIG=SIGKILL by ctypes and a raised oom_score_adj; it execs `/bin/sh -c COMMAND` with the given env, stdout/stderr to runs/RUN/out and runs/RUN/err. It holds the wall deadline (start + limits.wall, never moved) and the lease deadline read from `runs/RUN/deadline` every quarter second (an unreadable or unparsable file keeps the last value), both on CLOCK_BOOTTIME (Linux) or the platform's suspend-counting monotonic clock elsewhere; at the earlier one, or when `runs/RUN/stop` appears (with its grace), SIGTERM to the group, SIGKILL K seconds later (K from the stop file or grace(ttl)/4), and writes `exit` with the code and how (`exit`, `TERM`, `KILL`, `wall`, `lease`). After the end it waits for `runs/RUN/done` or a day (a hidden `--day SECONDS` for tests), removes its run folder by name after resolving it under the root, and exits. `kill` from the engine writes the stop file. `ended` is sent when the exit file appears (resources and output come in later gaps).

Definition of done.
1. A run started over the pipe executes, writes out/err/exit, and the worker answers `started` then `ended` with its exit code.
2. Closing the worker's stdin mid-run leaves the run going; its keeper kills it at its wall time and removes its folder after the (shortened) day.
3. SIGKILL of the keeper on Linux kills the run's first process (death signal); the test is skipped elsewhere.
4. A garbage deadline file never moves the kill later.
5. `kill` with a grace ends the run with SIGTERM, and with SIGKILL if it ignores TERM.
6. A bad run id, a full node and limits over the node are refused, and nothing is made for them.

Files: ergostat/compute/worker.py, tests/test_compute_keeper.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

Acceptance tests (at most 8 processes per test, all killed in teardown).

gaps.name: compute-worker-output
gaps.title: A node run's output sent by offset, resumed by attach, capped
gaps.definition:
Problem. The engine records a run's lines as it reads them from a file it follows (ergostat/spec/stream.py:27-62); over a session that can be cut, lines must be addressable so a resend is recorded once (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.3; ordering by offset, never time, the review lessons' lesson-2).

Change. In ergostat/compute/worker.py: a follower over each running run's `out` and `err` sends `out {run, stream, offset, text}` (offset of the first byte; at most 64 KiB a line, split at a line end where possible, else at the limit; whole lines only until the run ends). `attach {run, out, err}` resends from those offsets; `beat` carries each run's offsets taken (from the engine's last attach/ack). Flow control: at most 4 MiB sent ahead of the engine's acknowledged offsets, across runs, so a slow engine slows sending, never the worker's memory. A file past `limits.log` (default 64 MiB, at most 1 GiB) stops its run through the stop file with how `log over its cap`. `ended` comes after the last `out` of that run. `done {run}` writes runs/RUN/done. The rule that a line below the taken offset is dropped is shown in tests/compute_pipe.py; the engine's own use comes with compute-remote-backend.

Definition of done.
1. A run printing 10,000 lines yields offsets that cover out and err exactly once each, in order.
2. An attach from a middle offset resends from there; lines below it are not resent.
3. A line longer than 64 KiB arrives split, rejoined exactly by offset.
4. With the reader stalled, the worker holds at most 4 MiB unacknowledged and its RSS stays bounded (measured).
5. A run over its log cap is stopped and ended with that how.

gaps.name: compute-worker-readings
gaps.title: Per-run CPU and memory on the node, in beats and at the end
gaps.definition:
Problem. A local run's CPU and memory come from the shared sampler and the wait status (ergostat/costs/sampler.py:1-24, engine.py:1082-1089) and are written on agent.ran/agent.failed as `resources`. A node run has neither (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.8).

Change. In ergostat/compute/worker.py (standard library only; the sampler module cannot be imported, so a small tree sampler is written for the worker): each process-backend run's tree (its process group and descendants by parent), from /proc on Linux, one `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,rss=,utime=,stime=` elsewhere, sampled once a second for the first ten seconds then every ten; per run the CPU seconds, peak resident memory and peak process count. The latest per run is in each `beat`; the whole is in `ended.resources` with the same keys a local run's `resources` carries (as named in sampler.Sampler.finish, sampler.py:235). One sampling thread for all runs. Readings are measurements: nothing here becomes an event.

Definition of done.
1. A run that burns CPU for 2 s reports at least 1.5 CPU seconds in `ended.resources`.
2. A run that allocates 100 MB reports a peak at least that.
3. The keys of `ended.resources` equal those of a local run's resources.
4. One thread samples every run (a test counts threads with 4 runs going).

Files: ergostat/compute/worker.py, tests/test_compute_readings.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

Acceptance tests.
- tests/test_compute_readings.py::test_cpu_seconds_reported, ::test_memory_peak_reported, ::test_resource_keys_match_local, ::test_one_sampling_thread.

gaps.name: compute-worker-restart-states
gaps.title: A starting worker lists its runs as running, gone or unknown, and sweeps by name
gaps.definition:
Problem. A worker started again on a node must say which runs it still holds and what became of them, and must never call a run gone on a reading it did not make (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md sections 2.4 and 2.9; lesson-3 and lesson-6 on failed readings; lesson-11 deletes by allowlist). Today's local record decides `alive` by pid and start time only (ergostat/spec/runrecord.py:75-80) and reads an unread start time as gone.

Change. In ergostat/compute/worker.py: at start, read every `runs/RUN/` folder whose name matches `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`; each run is `running` (its pid alive with the recorded start time, or its container running with the id recorded, once docker exists), `gone` only on an allowlisted reading (the exit file written; or the pid absent or with another start time and its process group read as empty), else `unknown` (record unreadable, start time not read, `ps` failed or timed out, group not read, run alive but keeper gone). `hello.runs` lists them with their state; `beat` carries each state. For `unknown`, the worker at once stops the run by name itself (SIGTERM then SIGKILL to the group in runs/RUN/pgid) and keeps listing it unknown until a reading moves it. A keeper gone with its run ended: the worker records the missing exit and does the keeper's cleanup. A sweep at start and hourly removes only run folders of that name form under its root, each resolved and checked to be inside the root before deletion, and only when `done` exists or a day has passed since the run's end; it never deletes all-but-a-list.

Definition of done.
1. A run left running by a killed worker is listed `running` by the next.
2. A run whose exit file exists is `gone` with its exit.
3. A `ps` that fails (patched) gives `unknown`, never `gone`; the worker then signals the recorded group.
4. A reused pid (another start time) with the group empty gives `gone`; with the group not empty gives `unknown` and the group stopped.
5. The sweep leaves a folder named otherwise, a symlink pointing out of the root, and a folder of an un-done run younger than a day.

gaps.name: compute-worker-lease-clock
gaps.title: The worker turns the engine's lease renewals into its keeper's deadline, on its own clock
gaps.definition:
Problem. A keeper must kill a run whose lease the engine stopped renewing, by the engine's expiry, without ever comparing a time of the engine's with one of its own (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.7, *How the worker times it*; lesson-2). compute-worker-keeper reads `runs/RUN/deadline` but only its first value is written.

Change. In ergostat/compute/worker.py: each message from the engine that carries `sent` (start's lease, `renew {run, fence, left, sent}`, ping) gives `heard - sent` (heard on the worker's suspend-counting clock); `base` is the least of those over the last ten minutes. A run's lease deadline is `sent + base + left` of the latest renewal heard for its fence, converted to the keeper's clock and written to runs/RUN/deadline by temporary file and os.replace. A renewal of an older fence is ignored; a later renewal of the same fence may move the deadline either way, since the engine's `left` is authoritative. Only a renewal heard writes the file; a cut session writes nothing. K = grace(ttl)/4 with grace(ttl) = max(1, min(0.1 x ttl, 30)) (ergostat/leases/terms.py:38-41) is written beside the deadline for the keeper's SIGKILL.

Definition of done.
1. With renewals arriving at random delays (0-500 ms, patched clock), the deadline written is never later than the engine's expiry plus the least delay seen.
2. A worker whose clock of day is set an hour off (time.time patched) writes the same deadline.
3. A renewal delayed in the pipe does not move the deadline later than a prompt one would.
4. A renewal for an older fence is ignored.
5. No renewal after a cut session: the keeper kills by the last deadline plus K.

gaps.name: compute-node-connection
gaps.title: The engine's connection to each node of a pool: session, hello, beats, loss, round trips
gaps.definition:
Problem. The engine has no way to reach a worker (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md sections 2.1, 3, milestone gap 4). Remote systems use HTTP (ergostat/remote/); compute uses JSON lines over `ssh -T -o BatchMode=yes HOST ergostat worker --stdio`, or a pool's `connect:` argv.

Change. `ergostat/compute/connection.py`: one `Node` per entry of each pool the model declares (named `POOL/N`, by its place in the list, never by host), started by the engine when it starts and closed on close/swap: a subprocess with stdin/stdout pipes, one reader thread per node, the stderr kept in the pool's log under the state folder. It parses `hello` (version 1 only, else `error` said in the pool's status and nothing started there; labels must include the pool's `labels:`, else the node is not used), counts beats, and marks the node lost after three beats missed (30 s) or EOF, whichever first; reconnects with backoff from 1 s doubling to ten minutes. It sends `ping` every 2 s and keeps round trips on its own monotonic clock; `least_rtt(window=60)` is exposed. `request(msg) -> reply` with ids and a timeout; `on(type, fn)` for unsolicited lines (out, beat, ended). Per pool a `status()` dict (nodes in service, lost, slots, free, last error) is put in the engine's heartbeat and in `/api/status` under `compute` (ergostat/web/server.py:447-455), only when the model has pools. At most 64 nodes over all pools (compute-pools-config refuses more).

Definition of done.
1. A pool with `connect: [python3, -I, .../worker.py, --stdio, --root, R]` comes up: its node is in service with the worker's slots.
2. Killing the worker marks the node lost at EOF; a worker that stops beating (SIGSTOP) is lost after three missed beats.
3. A lost node is retried with backoff and comes back in service when the worker returns.
4. A worker answering another `v` leaves the pool's status with the error and no node in service.
5. `/api/status` shows `compute` only for a model with pools; a model without is unchanged.
6. No host name, address or user appears in status, logs or events (a node is POOL/N).

gaps.name: compute-capacity-measures
gaps.title: A pool's slots as built-in measures, and the dispatcher's room capped by them
gaps.definition:
Problem. A pool's capacity must read like any stock so a controller can hold a queue against it, and the dispatcher must stop sending to a pool whose slots are gone (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 4, *Compute capacity as a stock*; section 3's engine-wide 256). A block's room is its pool less its runs (ergostat/leases/dispatch.py:193-203), a daemon's capped by its free room (dispatch.py:197-198).

A lost node's slots leave `slots`/`free` at once. No diagram changes: a model may declare a stock on these measures and it is drawn as any stock (invariant 12).

1. Each measure reads the connections' numbers, per pool with `@POOL` and summed without.
2. A block on a pool with 2 free slots and pool 8 takes at most 2 items in a pass.
3. A node lost drops `slots@POOL` by its slots at the next reading, and no item is taken for it.

gaps.name: compute-remote-backend
gaps.title: A block with runs-on runs on a pool's node through the runner interface
gaps.definition:
Problem. With the interface, the spec, the connection and the worker's output in place, nothing yet joins them: `runner(spec, block)` returns `local` always (compute-runner-interface), and a `runs-on` block still runs here (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md milestone gap 4, acceptance).

Change. `ergostat/compute/remote.py`: a `remote` backend of the Runner protocol over a pool's connection. `start(spec)` picks a node in service with a free slot (fewest runs first), sends `start` with the RunSpec as JSON (the allowlisted environment, never the engine's), and returns a handle holding the node and run; `refused` raises a `Refused` the engine turns into `outcome["nack"] = {why, after: POOL_FULL_AFTER, count: False}` as a full workspace pool does (ergostat/spec/engine.py:1170-1171), so a misconfigured node costs no attempt, and the refusal is said in the pool's status. `follow` takes `out` lines for the run in offset order, drops any below the offset taken, hands complete lines to `take` exactly as stream.follow does, keeps the offset taken in the run's record under the state folder after each batch is recorded, sends acks, and returns at `ended` (exit code and how; how `wall` gives the note `stopped after its timeout of Ns`). `kill` sends `kill {run, why, grace}`; `alive` is the node's last beat for the run; `resources` is `ended.resources`; `cleanup` sends `done`. `runner()` returns it for a block whose `runs_on` names a pool. The run's note and exit are recorded by `_ran` unchanged.

Definition of done.
1. A program block with `runs-on: farm` over a same-machine worker (`connect:`) runs, and its agent.started/agent.ran records and its item's moves equal those of the same block run locally (ids and times aside).
2. Its lines are recorded once each even when the test forces a resend from an earlier offset.
3. A `start` refused (`full`, `no such image`) gives the item back uncounted and put off; the attempt count is unchanged.
4. A lease kill reaches the node run and records ergostat.run.killed with the signal the worker reports.
5. A block without `runs-on` is unchanged (the existing suites pass).

gaps.name: compute-lease-renew-on-node
gaps.title: A node run's lease renewed by the same activity as a local run's, killed on the node when not
gaps.definition:
Problem. The watchdog renews a local run's lease by activity only at its look, after the expiry (ergostat/leases/dispatch.py:458, 470-476, activity at 506-525). A node's keeper kills at the expiry (compute-worker-lease-clock), so a node run kept alive only by activity the fold does not count would be killed before the watchdog renews it (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.7, *What renews a node run's lease, and when*, *What the engine checks*; milestone gap 5).

Change. In ergostat/compute/remote.py and ergostat/leases/dispatch.py: for each run on a node, the engine sends `renew {run, fence, left, sent}` at once after any move of the lease's expiry in the fold and every 2 s besides (`left` = expiry less now, `sent` = its monotonic clock, read together). On each 2 s tick while the lease has less than half its TTL left, it calls `activity()` for the lease as the watchdog does; activity later than the lease's `renewed` records the same `renewed` event the watchdog would (`seen: activity`, at the activity's time, dispatch.py:474-475), at most one a tick per run, and the renew carries the new expiry. Before sending `start`, the node's least round trip over the last minute must be at most grace(ttl)/4 for the block's TTL (ergostat/leases/terms.py:38-41), else the item goes back uncounted as `full`; a running node run whose node's round trips grow past it is killed by `kill`. The fence and the watchdog are unchanged.

Definition of done.
1. A session cut and its worker ended: the run's keeper has SIGKILLed it by the expiry plus grace(ttl)/2, before the watchdog expires the lease; the item goes back once; a line the run's node sends after reconnecting is refused by the fence.
2. A node run whose only activity is events it causes about another item (one every third of its TTL; no line, no event about its own item) outlives its TTL several times, is never killed by its keeper, and ends agent.ran with renewed events `seen: activity`, as the same block run locally does.
3. The same run falling silent is killed by its keeper and its lease expires, counted.
4. A node whose round trip is past the bound is sent no start; the item goes back uncounted.
5. Renewals recorded: at most one per run per tick, none without new activity.

Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/leases/dispatch.py, ergostat/compute/connection.py, tests/test_compute_lease_on_node.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

gaps.name: compute-reattach
gaps.title: A cut session to a node is resumed: held runs attached from their offsets, others killed
gaps.definition:
Problem. When the SSH session to a node ends and comes back within one engine process, the runs on it keep going (compute-worker-keeper) but the engine's `follow` for each has lost its stream, and a run the engine no longer holds a lease for must never be left running on a node (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.4, last paragraph; milestone gap 6, the node half; the engine-restart half is compute-adopt-node-runs).

Change. In ergostat/compute/remote.py: on a node's `hello` after a reconnect, for each run listed: held by a lease of this engine (in `dispatch.mine`, fence matching) and `running` or `gone`, send `attach {run, out, err}` from the offsets in the run's record, and the waiting `follow` resumes, recording each line once and the end as usual; not held, send `kill` then `done` once ended; `unknown`, keep the lease, record no end, send no renewal, so the lease expires through the watchdog (ergostat/leases/dispatch.py:468-504) and the run ends agent.failed with the note `unknown on its node`. A run the engine follows that the hello does not list is ended with the note `lost on its node` only when its lease has expired (never released early on a reading not made, lesson-6).

Definition of done.
1. A session cut (connect process killed) mid-run and reconnected: every line is recorded exactly once and the run ends agent.ran with its exit.
2. A run listed by the node with no lease of ours is killed and its folder removed.
3. A run listed unknown keeps its lease until the watchdog expires it; it ends agent.failed `unknown on its node`; no renew is sent for it meanwhile.
4. A run missing from the hello is not ended before its lease's expiry.

Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/compute/connection.py, tests/test_compute_reattach.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

gaps.name: compute-adopt-node-runs
gaps.title: An engine started again takes up the runs on nodes its record says it started
gaps.definition:
Problem. After an engine restart no `_ran` thread waits for a run it had started, so nothing records that run's end; SPEC says taking up a run left behind by a stopped engine is not built (docs/SPEC.md:2379-2380; the proposal cites the old line 2201). `gap/rs-adopt-continued` (parked) builds that for local runs; node runs need the same, through the same mechanism (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.4 last paragraph, milestone gap 6).

Change. Extend whatever rs-adopt-continued lands (its adoption of a run found in the record with its lease held) to node runs: a node run's record (pool, node index, run id, fence, offsets taken; written by compute-remote-backend) is read at engine start; once the node's hello lists the run, the engine starts a follow thread for it through the remote backend's handle exactly as compute-reattach does, recording its lines from the offset taken and its end, its lease kept and renewed (compute-lease-renew-on-node). A run in the record whose node never comes back keeps its lease until the watchdog expires it. The end is recorded before the run's record file is released (the parked rs-adopt review's finding).

Definition of done.
1. An engine killed while a node run goes, and started again: the run's remaining lines are recorded once, its end is agent.ran, its item moves as a run that was never interrupted.
2. A node run whose node is gone at restart ends only when its lease expires, counted.
3. Local and node runs are adopted by one code path (one function the two backends' handles share).
4. SPEC 2379-2380's sentence is replaced by what is built.

gaps.name: compute-secrets
gaps.title: A pool's secrets read from files, sent at start, never written by ergostat
gaps.definition:
Problem. A local run inherits the engine's whole environment (ergostat/spec/engine.py:995), so every secret the engine was started with reaches every run, and nothing says a run needs one. A node run gets only the allowlisted environment (compute-run-spec), so it has no way to receive a secret (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.6; milestone gap 8).

Change. The pool's `secrets: {NAME: file}` (compiled by compute-pools-config) are read at each start by the remote backend (`~` expanded; an unreadable file refuses the start, said by name, item given back uncounted) and sent in `start.secrets`. The worker keeps them in memory only: the process backend adds them to the run's environment in the keeper's exec (passed to the keeper through an inherited pipe, never a file or argv); the docker backend (later) passes `-e NAME` with the value in the docker client's environment. The worker replaces each secret's exact value in forwarded lines with `[secret NAME]` (a second layer only). Records, events, run.json, beats and errors carry names only; agent.started gets `secrets: [names]`.

Definition of done.
1. After a run that prints nothing secret, the secret's value is in no file under the worker's root, the engine's state folder, the event record or any log (a test walks them all and greps for the value).
2. The run sees the secret in its environment; agent.started names it.
3. A run that prints the secret has the line recorded with `[secret NAME]`.
4. An unreadable secret file refuses the start, uncounted, with the name and not the path's contents.

Files: ergostat/compute/remote.py, ergostat/compute/worker.py, tests/test_compute_secrets.py (new), docs/SPEC.md.

Acceptance tests.
- tests/test_compute_secrets.py::test_secret_never_written, ::test_secret_reaches_run_and_name_recorded, ::test_printed_secret_masked, ::test_unreadable_secret_refuses_start.

gaps.name: compute-work-in
gaps.title: A node run starts in a worktree at an exact commit sent as a git bundle
gaps.definition:
Problem. A node run has an empty folder: it cannot work on the model's repository (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.5, *In: an exact commit*; milestone gap 7, first half). Locally, workspace pools make worktrees (ergostat/workspaces/git.py:50-58).

Change. RunSpec.work = {repo, commit} (a name in the pool's `repos:`, and a commit id, never a branch), set when the block says `work: {repo, commit: FIELD}` naming an item field that holds the commit (one block key added to compute-pools-config's compiler here). The worker keeps one bare repository per name under its root (`repos/NAME.git`), answers `need {repo, commit, have: [newest commits]}` when it lacks the commit; the engine makes `git bundle create` of what is missing (`--not` the haves), sends it as `bundle` chunks of at most 1 MiB, at most 2 GiB in all, with size and SHA-256; the worker verifies, fetches it and makes the run's folder a detached worktree at that commit. Bare repositories are pruned by age and a disk cap (`--keep`).

Definition of done.
1. A run with work at commit C sees the tree at C (a test checks a file's content and `git rev-parse HEAD`).
2. A second run at a later commit sends only the missing commits (the bundle is smaller; checked).
3. A bundle with a wrong hash or over the cap is refused; the start is refused uncounted.
4. A branch name in place of a commit is refused at check or start.
5. Pruning removes only repositories under repos/ of the name form.

gaps.name: compute-work-out
gaps.title: A node run's commits, artifacts and transcripts brought back, hashed, capped and fenced
gaps.definition:
Problem. What a node run makes stays on the node and is removed with its folder (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.5, *Out*; milestone gap 7, second half). The factory's containers bring work out as a git bundle made with no network (dev/bin/agents.py:309-335), unreachable from a model.

Change. RunSpec.out = {bundle, artifacts: [globs], transcripts: [globs]} from the block's `out:` (key added here). When the run ends the worker makes a git bundle of the commits on top of the given commit, collects files matching the globs inside the run folder only (symlinks resolving outside refused, said), and sends each as `result` chunks with size and SHA-256, capped (bundle 256 MiB, artifacts 1 GiB, transcripts 64 MiB by default). The engine verifies each, fetches the bundle into a side ref `refs/ergostat/runs/RUN-FENCE` of the named repository (never a branch), and keeps the rest under `runs/RUN/` in the state folder; agent.ran carries their names, sizes and hashes. A result arriving after the run's lease ended is refused by the fence and said. `done` is sent only after the results are kept.

Definition of done.
1. A run that commits twice has its commits at the side ref, and no branch moved.
2. An artifact glob brings back the matching files byte-exact; a symlink out of the folder is refused and named.
3. Over a cap: refused, the run's end notes it.
4. A result after the lease ended is refused and recorded as refused.

gaps.name: compute-docker-backend
gaps.title: The worker's Docker backend: a run in a named container under its limits
gaps.definition:
Problem. The process backend cannot limit network or isolate files (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 2.2, *docker*; milestone gap 9). The factory already runs its sessions in containers with hard limits and `--init` (dev/bin/agents.py:53-54), secrets by name (agents.py:12-14, 145-155) and kill by name (agents.py:161-164), but only for itself.

Change. In ergostat/compute/worker.py: backend `docker` when `docker` is on PATH (`hello.backends`, and `hello.images` from `docker image ls`). The keeper runs `docker run -d --init --name ergostat-run-RUN --cpus --memory --memory-swap(=memory) --pids-limit --network none(default) --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges -v RUNFOLDER:/work -w /work IMAGE /bin/sh -c COMMAND`, output to the run folder's out/err files (a wrapper in the container redirects; never `docker logs` alone), records the container id in run.json, waits with `docker wait`, writes the exit; at its deadlines `docker stop -t K` then `docker rm -f`. Readings from the container's cgroup (cpu.stat, memory.current, memory.peak), in the same keys as the process backend. `no such image` is refused at start. restart-states reads a container as running or exited by its recorded id (the docker reading added to its allowlist). The sweep removes only containers named `ergostat-run-` plus 32 hex. Docker is a resource limit, not a security boundary (CLAUDE.md): the SPEC says so.

Definition of done.
1. A docker run's output, exit and readings arrive as a process run's do.
2. With `network: none`, a run that opens a socket fails.
3. After a session is cut, the keeper has asked `docker rm -f` by the lease's expiry plus grace(ttl)/2.
4. `no such image` is refused before anything is made.
5. Tests skip when docker is absent.

gaps.name: compute-calls-from-node
gaps.title: A node run calls the engine back through a socket its worker forwards
gaps.definition:
Problem. A local run calls `ergostat act`, `event --add`, `lease` and `item` through `ERGOSTAT_SOCKET` (ergostat/spec/engine.py:1005-1008, 1817-1819; ergostat/calls/). On a node there is no such socket, so compute-pools-config refuses every `runs-on` block whose command uses calls (docs/proposals/compute-systems.md section 4, milestone gap 10).

Change. The worker serves a Unix socket in each run's folder (`runs/RUN/calls.sock`, mounted for docker), puts its path in the run's `ERGOSTAT_SOCKET`, and forwards each call as `call {run, id, body}` to the engine, at most 20 calls a second a run (beyond: answered `busy`). The engine answers it as its own socket does (ergostat/calls/server.py's handler, with the run's identity from the handle, never from the call), and the worker relays `answer`. `ERGOSTAT_CMD` on a node names `python3 -I worker.py --call` (a client mode of the worker that speaks the same socket protocol as ergostat/calls/client.py). compute-pools-config's refusal is lifted for program blocks.

Definition of done.
1. A node run that calls `$ERGOSTAT_CMD event --add` gets its event recorded, caused by its run, as a local run's is.
2. A call naming another run's identity is answered as the caller's run, never the claimed one.
3. The 21st call in a second is answered `busy`.
4. A call arriving after the run's lease ended is refused by the fence as a local one is.
5. check no longer refuses `runs-on` blocks that call.

gaps.name: conformance-list-files
gaps.title: Conformance lists: a list file read and validated, every limit refused by name
gaps.definition:
# conformance-list-files: a conformance list file is read and validated, and a bad one is refused by name

depends-on: []

The owner (2026-11-21) wants the features we wish we had listed, each tested, and the passing count kept as a stock. docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 1 defines the list file: `list`, `description`, `cases` (each with `check`, `timeout`, `asked`, `from`, `description`). Its limits are names matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, at most 500 cases in a list, at most 20 lists and 500 cases across one use, a timeout of at most 10m (default 1m), and each list's `list:` equal to its file name. Nothing on main reads such a file. The only list of cases today is hand-written inside one demo's runner (`examples/image-squeeze/world/bench.py:43-60`), and the library's programs live in `ergostat/library/run/` (`ergostat/library/run/__init__.py:1-17`). Every later conformance gap (the runner, ergostat's three lists) needs one reader that says yes or no in the same way. Proposal section 2, step 1: if any named list cannot be read, the run stops and no case moves.

## Change
A small, pure module `ergostat/library/run/conformance_lists.py`:
- `read(folder, names) -> Lists`: reads `<folder>/<name>.yaml` for each name, in order. It raises `ListError(name, why)` on the first problem.
- `Case(list, name, id, check, timeout_s, asked, from_, description)`, with `id = case/<list>/<name>`.
- `Lists.cases` (in file order), `Lists.declared` (the count) and `Lists.digest` (a sha256 over the files' bytes in name order, which the runner uses to tell an edited list).
- It never touches the model loader: lists are not model files.

## Definition of done
1. `read` returns every case of every named list, in order, with defaults filled in (`timeout` 1m, `asked` true).
2. Each of these is refused with the list's name and a reason naming the key: a missing file; YAML that is not a mapping; `list:` not equal to the file name; a name repeated in `names`; a list or case name off the pattern; a case without `check`; a timeout unparseable or over 10m; `asked` not a bool; an unknown key; more than 500 cases in one list; more than 20 lists; more than 500 cases across them.
3. Durations are parsed by `ergostat.durations.parse_duration`, not by a new parser.
4. `digest` changes when any named file's bytes change, and not when a file outside `names` changes.
5. The module imports nothing from `ergostat.spec` beyond durations, and is under 140 lines.

gaps.name: conformance-runner-runs-cases
gaps.title: Conformance runner: runs each case in its own process group and reports met, unmet or broken
gaps.definition:
# conformance-runner-runs-cases: `${lib} conformance` runs every case of every list and reports each as an observation

depends-on: [conformance-list-files]

The proposal's runner (docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 2, steps 1-4, 6 and 7) does not exist. The library's program table is fixed in `ergostat/library/run/__main__.py:9-12`, and `conformance` is not in it. Two engine facts shape it:
- A `run` sensor's timeout kills only the process it started and returns (`ergostat/spec/engine.py:2402-2406`). Whatever a check started would keep running (lesson 6).
- A sensor that exits non-zero records neither its reading nor its observations (`ergostat/spec/engine.py:2407-2410`).

Observation lines need an item id with a `/` and an event type that is not ergostat's own (`ergostat/spec/engine.py:2340-2345`). `case.met`, `case.unmet` and `case.broken` pass. The demo's runner shows the pattern of measuring again only when the code moved (`examples/image-squeeze/world/bench.py:43-46`).

## Change
A new `ergostat/library/run/conformance.py`, registered as `conformance` in `__main__.py` and listed in `ergostat/library/run/__init__.py`'s docstring:

`conformance --folder F --lists NAME [--lists NAME ...] [--when CMD] [--budget SECONDS] [--instance NAME]`

1. It reads the lists with `conformance_lists.read`. On a `ListError` it prints the reason to stderr and exits 2, running nothing.
2. It works out the key: the stdout of `--when` (if given) and the lists' digest. If the key equals the last run's, kept with `common.kept(instance, "runs")`, it prints only the declared count and exits 0.
3. Otherwise it increments the run counter kept beside the key. Then it runs each case one at a time, `shell=True`, in the project's folder, with `start_new_session=True`. At the case's timeout it kills the whole process group (`os.killpg`, SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2s). Exit 0 is met, exit 1 is unmet, anything else, a timeout or a command that cannot start is broken.
4. It stops starting cases once the budget left is less than the next case's timeout. Each case not run is named on stderr, prints no line and keeps its last state.
5. For each case run it prints one line: `{"event": "case.met|case.unmet|case.broken", "item": "case/<list>/<name>", "data": {list, asked, description, from, run, key, said}}`. `data.list` comes from the id's prefix. `said` is the last 20 lines (at most 2000 chars) of the check's output, for unmet and broken only.
6. It prints the declared count across all lists as its last line and exits 0 whatever the cases said.

## Definition of done
1. Points 1-6 above hold, each with a test.
2. A hung check that has started a child is killed with its child: no process of its group is left after the case's timeout plus 3s.
3. Run numbers rise by one per real run and never repeat, so "newer" is read by sequence, never by time (lesson 2).
4. The program imports only `common`, `conformance_lists` and the standard library.

## Files to touch
`ergostat/library/run/conformance.py` (new), `ergostat/library/run/__main__.py`, `ergostat/library/run/__init__.py`, `tests/test_conformance_runner.py` (new).

## Risks
- lesson-6: kill the group, not the pid.
- lesson-3: a list that cannot be read exits non-zero, so the engine records no reading instead of 0.

## Acceptance tests
- test_exit_0_met_exit_1_unmet_exit_2_broken
- test_missing_command_is_broken
- test_hung_check_killed_with_its_children
- test_unreadable_list_runs_nothing_and_exits_nonzero
- test_same_key_prints_count_only
- test_edited_list_reruns_with_same_when_key
- test_out_of_budget_names_skipped_cases_and_prints_no_line_for_them
- test_run_number_rises_per_real_run
- test_declared_count_is_last_line_and_exit_is_0_with_unmet_cases

gaps.name: conformance-runner-withdraws
gaps.title: Conformance runner: a case taken off its list, or a list dropped, is withdrawn
gaps.definition:
# conformance-runner-withdraws: case items no list declares any more are withdrawn by the runner

depends-on: [conformance-runner-runs-cases]

Without this, a case taken off a list stays `met` and keeps counting (docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 2 step 5, lesson 5). The runner from conformance-runner-runs-cases prints only the cases it ran. A sensor's command can read the record back through `$ERGOSTAT_CMD`, which the engine sets for every sensor (`ergostat/spec/engine.py:2359-2367`), with `item --kind case --json` (`docs/SPEC.md:1729`).

## Change
In `ergostat/library/run/conformance.py`, after the cases run (only on a real run, not on a repeated key):
- Read the items of kind `case` through `$ERGOSTAT_CMD item --kind case --json`.
- Print `{"event": "case.withdrawn", "item": id, "data": {list, run}}` for each item, not already `withdrawn`, whose id is `case/<list>/<name>` where either `<list>` was read and `<name>` is not in it, or `<list>` is not among `--lists`.
- Judge by the id's prefix, never by `data.list`.
- If the item read fails (no `$ERGOSTAT_CMD`, a non-zero exit, output that is not JSON), withdraw nothing and say so on stderr, but still exit 0 with the count: the cases' own results stand.
- An id not of the form `case/<list>/<name>` is left alone and named on stderr.

## Definition of done
1. A case removed from a read list is withdrawn once. A second run with the same lists does not withdraw it again.
2. With two lists, a case removed from one is withdrawn and the other list's items get no `case.withdrawn`.
3. A list dropped from `--lists` has every one of its items withdrawn.
4. An unreadable list still stops the run before any withdrawal (inherited from step 1; tested here).
5. A failed item read withdraws nothing and does not change the exit code.

## Files to touch
`ergostat/library/run/conformance.py`, `tests/test_conformance_runner.py`.

## Risks
- lesson-5: an item judged by the wrong list would be withdrawn while still declared. Use the id's prefix only.

## Acceptance tests

- test_two_lists_removal_touches_only_its_list
- test_dropped_list_cases_withdrawn

gaps.definition:
# conformance-template: a built-in `use: conformance` makes the case kind, the count as a stock, its flows and three goals

depends-on: [conformance-runner-runs-cases]

Any project should be able to count its wishes without writing its own `bench.py`. Today the only model that does is hand-written (`examples/image-squeeze/benchmark.yaml:9-25`, `:57-72`, `:114-117`). The built-in templates are YAML files under `ergostat/library/templates/` (`ergostat/library/templates.py:1-6`, the head keys at `:24`). A `once: true` template keeps its parts' names, and a second use is refused as used-twice (`docs/SPEC.md:142-144`, `ergostat/library/uses.py:121`). Its parameters expand with `${folder:quote}` and `${lists:arg}` (`docs/SPEC.md:222-223`). A goal may hold at a level, `== 0` (`ergostat/spec/ir.py:686`). One name clash to avoid: "conformance suite" already means the storage backends' unit suite (`docs/SPEC.md:662`).

## Change
`ergostat/library/templates/conformance.yaml`, `once: true`, with section 2's body as written in the proposal:
- the item kind `case` (states `unmet, met, broken, withdrawn`; show `list, description, from, asked, run, key, said`);
- the stocks `conformance-declared` (the runner's number), `conformance-met` and `conformance-wanted` (`items:` sensors);
- the auxiliary `conformance-unaccounted`;
- the flows `conformance-gained` and `conformance-lost`;
- the goals `every-wish` (`<= 0`), `nothing-lost` (`<= 0`) and `every-case-run` (`== 0`).

Its parameters:
- `folder` (path, required);
- `lists` (names, required);
- `when` (command, optional, passed as `--when`);
- `every` (duration, default 10m);
- `timeout` (duration, default 30m: the run sensor's timeout, and passed as `--budget ${timeout:seconds}`).

The template also has `reading:`, `example:` and a stand-in: with no lists given, it is a list folder inside the template (two cases, `true` and `false`) so the template runs offline like the others. A section in SPEC §2a and in `docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md` says how to use it, says "conformance list" (never "suite") for the new thing, and gives the per-list count recipe (`where: {list: NAME}`, proposal section 3).

## Definition of done
1. A model with one `use: conformance` naming the stand-in passes `ergostat check` with no new finding, and the Dynamics view draws `conformance-met` with its two flows.
2. A second `use: conformance` in one model is refused as used-twice.
3. After a run of the stand-in, `conformance-met` reads 1, `conformance-wanted` 1, `conformance-declared` 2 and `conformance-unaccounted` 0. `every-wish` is off and `every-case-run` holds.
4. A case item pushed by hand that no list declares makes `conformance-unaccounted` -1 and puts `every-case-run` off.
5. A declared case never run makes `conformance-unaccounted` above 0, and `every-case-run` off.
6. The sensor command the template writes passes `--budget` equal to the sensor's own timeout in seconds.

## Files to touch
`ergostat/library/templates/conformance.yaml` (new), the stand-in list files beside it, `docs/SPEC.md` (§2a), `docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md`, `tests/test_conformance_template.py` (new).

## Risks
- lesson-3: the count's sensor is the `items:` count, never the runner, so a failed run leaves the count at its last value.

## Acceptance tests
- test_template_checks_clean_with_standin
- test_second_use_refused_used_twice
- test_standin_run_counts_met_wanted_declared
- test_unlisted_case_item_puts_every_case_run_off
- test_never_run_case_puts_every_case_run_off
- test_budget_equals_sensor_timeout

The factory never lets an AI change main directly. Work arrives as gaps. The simplifier shows how a program asks for one: pool 1 under a lock, the open gaps read again under it, a definition written and `gap.requested` recorded with `source` (`dev/bin/simplify.py:147-173`, the add at `:167`). The proposal's loop (docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 4, milestone gap 3) asks the same way for an unmet case. Case items exist once conformance-factory-model runs. The gap kind is declared at `ergostat.yaml:85`, and a kind may declare typed relations (`docs/SPEC.md:1222`, as `removal` does at `dev/model/code-health.yaml:27-28`).

## Change
A new `dev/bin/conformance.py` with subcommands `request` and `in-flight`.
- `request`: under `run/conformance.lock` it reads the open gaps and the case items. It picks the unmet case with `asked: true` that has no gap in flight (by `case` field) and that has waited longest, by its item's first `case.unmet`. It writes a definition in the house shape: the problem (the case's `description` and `from`); the change left to the implementor; a definition of done whose first point is "`<check>` exits 0 on main"; the check named as the acceptance test; a size budget of 300. It then records `gap.requested` with `source: conformance`, `case: <case id>`, `title` and `definition`, the same way the simplifier does.
- `in-flight` prints the count of `source: conformance` gaps not merged, parked or closed.
- The gap kind in `ergostat.yaml` gains the relation `case: case`.

## Definition of done
1. With an unmet, asked case and none in flight, `request` records one gap whose definition names the case's check and cites its `from`.
2. With one conformance gap in flight, `request` asks for none.
3. A case with `asked: false`, or in state `broken` or `withdrawn`, is never chosen. A broken check is fixed by hand first.
4. Two `request` runs at once ask for at most one gap (the lock).
5. `in-flight` counts only `source: conformance` gaps in open-to-queued states.
6. The gap's item page shows the case as a related item.

## Files to touch
`dev/bin/conformance.py` (new), `ergostat.yaml` (the relation), `tests/test_conformance_requester.py` (new).

## Risks
- Reuse `dev/bin/fac.py`'s helpers (`fac.add`, `fac.rel`), not a second way to record.
- No machine names or user names in the generated definition.

## Acceptance tests
- test_request_asks_one_gap_naming_the_check
- test_no_request_while_one_in_flight
- test_not_asked_broken_withdrawn_never_chosen
- test_concurrent_requests_ask_once
- test_in_flight_counts_only_conformance_source

At most 160 net lines outside `tests/` (dev/ counts).

gaps.name: conformance-loop-wiring
gaps.title: The factory's loop that raises the conformance count: when to ask, and what was asked
gaps.definition:
# conformance-loop-wiring: `every-wish` off asks for a gap, paced like the simplifier

depends-on: [conformance-gap-requester]

After conformance-gap-requester, the program exists, but nothing runs it. The simplifier's wiring is the pattern to follow:
- an `expr` block computes wanted, nothing in flight and budget not spent (`dev/model/code-health.yaml:143-152`, the budget input `goal.ai-budget.off` at `:149`);
- a program block takes it (`:173-180`);
- an in-flight auxiliary is read from the program (`:43-47`);
- the gaps asked for are counted by source (`:132-136`).

The proposal's goal `every-wish` is meant to stay off while the list is open, so the loop is paced by pool 1 and the AI budget, not by the goal turning off (docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 4).

## Change
In `dev/model/conformance.yaml`, add:
- the auxiliary `conformance-requests-in-flight` (run `python3 dev/bin/conformance.py in-flight`, every 10m);
- the flow `conformance-requested` into `gaps-open` (system intake), with sensor `{items: gap, entering: open, where: {source: conformance}, over: 1d}`;
- the expr block `conformance-when`, inputs `goal.every-wish.off`, the in-flight auxiliary and `goal.ai-budget.off`, `expr: wanted * (inflight < 1) * (1 - over)`, out to `block.conformance-requester`;
- the program block `conformance-requester` (run `python3 dev/bin/conformance.py request`, every 6h, timeout 15m, out `flow.conformance-requested`);
- a line in `dev/README.md`'s conformance section.

## Definition of done
1. `ergostat check` gives no new finding, and the Blocks view draws the loop: `every-wish`'s junction, `conformance-when` and the requester.
2. Replayed with `every-wish` off, none in flight and the budget not spent, the requester is commanded. With the budget spent, or one in flight, it is not.
3. A gap the requester asks for shows on `conformance-requested`.
4. The flow names `gaps-open` as its stock, so the intake's balance is unchanged for other sources.

## Files to touch
`dev/model/conformance.yaml`, `dev/README.md`, `tests/test_factory.py` (a replay test of the command, as the simplifier's has, if one exists).

## Acceptance tests
- the requester is commanded only when wanted, none in flight and the budget not spent
- the flow counts only `source: conformance` gaps
- `ergostat check` reports no new finding

## Size budget
0 net lines of code outside `tests/`, `docs/` and `dev/`. The YAML is at most about 40 lines.

gaps.name: conformance-regressions-ask
gaps.title: A lost conformance case asks the coordinator, as the code measures do
gaps.definition:
# conformance-regressions-ask: `nothing-lost` off asks the coordinator through `factory-off`

depends-on: [conformance-factory-model]

A case that was met and stops being met is the flow `conformance-lost`. Its goal `nothing-lost` is off for a day (docs/proposals/conformance-stock.md section 4). Nothing acts on it yet. The factory's measures already have one commander for the coordinator: `code-health-off` feeds `factory-off` (`dev/model/code-health.yaml:163-172`), which asks the coordinator with a stated prompt (`dev/model/measures.yaml:132-153`). The image-squeeze rollout also refuses a candidate that loses a case (`examples/image-squeeze/benchmark.yaml:67-68`). Whether ergostat's merge queue should do the same is the owner's call (proposal, questions).

## Change
In `dev/model/conformance.yaml`, add an expr block `conformance-off` (system measures, beside `code-health-off`, so the link reaches `factory-off` from inside measures). Its input is `goal.nothing-lost.off`, `expr: lost`, out `block.factory-off`. `factory-off`'s `ask` text in `dev/model/measures.yaml` gains one clause: a lost conformance case is named by `ergostat item --kind case --state unmet` with its last `said`, and the coordinator requests a gap that restores it. This gap's record asks the owner in one sentence whether a merge that loses a met case should also be held by the merge queue. That is not built.

## Definition of done
1. `ergostat check` gives no new finding. In particular, no interface finding for a link into `measures`' internals.
2. Replayed with a met case moved to unmet, `nothing-lost` goes off and `factory-off` is commanded. With no loss, `conformance-off` is 0.
3. A case that moves from met to withdrawn does not put `nothing-lost` off. If it does (because `leaving: met` counts withdrawals), the flow's sensor is narrowed to cases entering `unmet` or `broken`, and the record says so.
4. The owner's question is written in the record, one sentence.

## Files to touch
`dev/model/conformance.yaml`, `dev/model/measures.yaml` (the ask text), `tests/test_factory.py` if a replay test is there.

## Risks
- lesson-5: a withdrawal is not a regression (point 3).

## Acceptance tests
- a met case lost puts nothing-lost off and commands factory-off
- a withdrawn case does not
- `ergostat check` reports no new finding

## Size budget
0 net lines of code outside `tests/`, `docs/` and `dev/`. The YAML is at most about 20 lines.

gaps.name: regression-queue-test-counts
gaps.title: The merge queue records each suite's pytest counts, unknown when its log cannot say
gaps.definition:
## Problem

The queue keeps only `rc`, `seconds` and, for the browser suite, a count of `SKIPPED` lines per suite (dev/bin/queue.py:111-114). Nothing records how many tests passed, failed, were skipped or deselected, so no measure can say main lost tests (the proposal's `tests-passing`, docs/proposals/regression-guarantees.md section 4 and milestone gap 1). The record lands on each gap as `suites_queue` (dev/bin/queue.py:671-674) and the run's entry in `queue_runs` (dev/bin/queue.py:836-837).

## Change

A pure parser `fac.counts(text)` next to `fac.outcomes` (dev/bin/fac.py:582-588) that reads pytest's final summary line (`N failed, N passed, N skipped, N deselected, N errors ... in Xs`, with or without the `=` padding) from the suite's **whole** log. It takes the last such line, never a tail. In `suites()`'s `one()` each pytest suite (unit, browser, host) gains `counts: {passed, failed, skipped, deselected, errors}`. A suite whose log has no summary line, was stopped by a sibling (`stopped_by`), stalled, or could not be read records `counts: "unknown"`, never zeros (lesson 3). ruff and demo record no counts. The landed run's `queue_runs` entry gains `counts` summed over unit, browser and host, or `"unknown"` if any of them is.

## Definition of done

1. `fac.counts` parses every summary form pytest -q prints, including xdist's, and returns None for text with no summary.
2. Each pytest suite in `suites_queue` carries `counts`, or `"unknown"`.
3. The landed run's `queue_runs` entry carries the summed `counts`, or `"unknown"`.
4. The existing `skipped` field and the browser rule that a skip fails the run (dev/bin/queue.py:111, 216-220) are unchanged.
5. dev/README.md names the new fields where the queue's record is described.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/fac.py, dev/bin/queue.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_queue.py.

## Acceptance tests

- `test_counts_from_a_summary_with_failures_and_skips`: a log ending `3 failed, 120 passed, 1 skipped, 4 deselected in 12.0s` records exactly those numbers.
- `test_a_truncated_log_records_unknown_never_zero`: a log cut before its summary records `"unknown"`.
- `test_a_stopped_sibling_records_unknown`: the suite stopped by another's failure records `"unknown"`.
- `test_the_last_summary_wins`: a log quoting an earlier summary in its output takes the last line.
- ruff clean, unit and browser suites rc 0.

## Size budget

60 net lines outside tests/ (all in dev/bin/).

gaps.name: regression-flake-writes-hold-state
gaps.title: A flake seen never takes a test out of main-broken, and a second break keeps the first clock
gaps.definition:
## Problem

The kind `flake` moves to `seen` on every `flake.seen` (ergostat.yaml:197-200). Four writers emit it without looking at the item: dev/bin/onmain.py:74, dev/bin/queue.py:241-242, dev/bin/triage.py:76 and dev/bin/manage.py:231. So a test still failing on main leaves `main-broken` and is counted as a flake. Every `flake.main-broken` writes a fresh `main_broken_at` (dev/bin/onmain.py:92-94), so a second gap hitting the same break on a newer main restarts the repair clock (lessons 2 and 5). A flake fixed and then seen again keeps its old `times` (fold `sum`, ergostat.yaml:202): the remake carries stale state (lesson 5).

## Change

A new module `dev/bin/flakes.py` with one writer, `flakes.say(event, test, **data)`, that every flake writer calls instead of `fac.say`. Under one lock file in the run dir (fcntl, the pattern of dev/bin/fac.py:346-358), it re-reads the item (`ergostat item flake/<slug> --json`) and writes synchronously with `fac.add` (dev/bin/fac.py:139-141), so check and write are one step (lesson 1):
- `flake.seen` on an item in `main-broken` writes `flake.measured` with the same data (counts `times`, moves no state).
- `flake.main-broken` on an item already in `main-broken` updates `main` to the newer sha and unions `gaps`, and leaves `main_broken_at` alone.
- `flake.seen` or `flake.main-broken` on an item in `fixed` is a remake: written as a `patch` changeset (docs/SPEC.md:1230-1235) that sets `times` to 1 and removes `main_fixed_at`, `fixed_by` and `green_passes`, with a new `main_broken_at` for a break.
- An item that cannot be read is written as today, and the failure is said on stderr. The kind's states are the safe default: a break is still recorded.
The four call sites switch to it. `flake.measured` is listed in the kind's comment as a no-state event.

## Definition of done

1. All four writers go through `flakes.say`, and no other code emits `flake.seen` or `flake.main-broken` (grep test).
2. A `seen` on a `main-broken` item leaves it `main-broken` and adds to `times`.
3. A second `main-broken` keeps the first `main_broken_at` and moves `main`.
4. A remake from `fixed` starts at `times` 1 with no `main_fixed_at`.
5. The lock is held across the read and the write. Two concurrent writers (threads in the test) never lose a state.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/flakes.py (new), dev/bin/onmain.py, dev/bin/queue.py, dev/bin/triage.py, dev/bin/manage.py, ergostat.yaml (the kind's comment), tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests

- `test_a_flake_seen_on_a_main_broken_item_keeps_it_main_broken`
- `test_a_second_break_keeps_the_first_clock_and_moves_main`
- `test_a_flake_seen_after_fixed_starts_a_new_count`
- `test_every_flake_writer_goes_through_the_helper`: no `fac.say("flake.seen"` or `"flake.main-broken"` left in dev/bin.
- `test_two_writers_under_the_lock_lose_nothing`: a `main-broken` and a `seen` racing on one item end `main-broken`.
- `ergostat check` on ergostat.yaml: no errors.

## Size budget

120 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: regression-flake-main-fixed
gaps.title: A test broken on main leaves main-broken when it passes twice alone on a newer main
gaps.definition:
## Problem

Nothing takes an item out of `main-broken`. The kind's only events are `seen`, `main-broken` and `fixed` (ergostat.yaml:197-200), the only writer of `main-broken` is dev/bin/onmain.py:94, and nothing ever emits `fixed`. A stock of tests failing on main would only rise, and a goal `main-green` could never recover (docs/proposals/regression-guarantees.md section 3, milestone gap 2).

## Change

- Declare `flake.main-fixed: fixed` on the kind.
- A new program `dev/bin/mend.py`, a block `main-mend` in dev/model/landing.yaml (`every: 30m`, pool 1, a lease, `timeout: 30m`). It fetches the pushed main (the pattern of dev/bin/upgrade.py:35-37) and waits for a quiet machine (`fac.wait_quiet`, as triage does). It then takes at most `[gates] mend_most` items in `main-broken`, oldest first (default 5, ceiling 20: lesson 4), and runs their tests alone twice on that sha in a suite container, the way `onmain.failing` does (dev/bin/onmain.py:47-54), with `-rA`. Each result comes from `fac.outcomes` over the whole log (dev/bin/fac.py:582-588).
- A test that passed both runs gets `flake.main-fixed` with `passed_on` (the sha), `main_fixed_at` and `fixed_by: main-mend`. It is written as a `patch` changeset whose first op is `{"op": "test", "path": "/main", "value": <the item's main as read>}` (docs/SPEC.md:1230-1243). It is written only if that `main` is `passed_on` or an ancestor of it (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`), so a newer break written in between refuses it (lessons 1 and 2).
- A test that failed, was skipped, was not collected or is quarantined (`fac.quarantine` on that sha), or a run that could not be read, is unknown and stays `main-broken`, as quarantine scoring counts it (dev/bin/fac.py:582-588; lesson 3).

## Definition of done

1. `flake.main-fixed` is declared and moves the item to `fixed`.
2. `main-mend` runs on its schedule, waits for a quiet machine, and checks at most `mend_most` tests a run.
3. Only two passes on the pushed main clear an item. Unknown never does.
4. A break written between the read and the write is kept: the refused changeset leaves the item `main-broken`. The test checks that a refused patch also refuses the state move.
5. dev/README.md describes the block next to the merge queue's.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/mend.py (new), dev/model/landing.yaml, ergostat.yaml, dev/factory.toml (`[gates] mend_most`), dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests

- `test_main_fixed_after_two_passes_alone`
- `test_a_skipped_or_unreadable_run_stays_main_broken`
- `test_a_quarantined_test_is_never_cleared_by_mend`
- `test_a_newer_break_between_check_and_write_is_kept` (the `test` op refuses it)
- `test_mend_checks_at_most_mend_most`
- `ergostat check`: no errors.

## Size budget

150 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: regression-flake-fixed-after-green
gaps.title: A seen flake is fixed after N green queue runs that each say it passed
gaps.definition:
## Problem

`flake.fixed` is declared (ergostat.yaml:200) and emitted nowhere, so no flake ever leaves `seen`: the state fills and never drains (proposal section 3, F4/F9 row, and milestone gap 2). The queue's green runs could clear them, but its unit and browser commands print no PASSED lines (`-rfEs` and `-rs`, dev/factory.toml:158 and :170). A deleted or renamed flake would then count as "passed" in every green run, which fails open (lesson 3).

## Change

- Add `p` to the `-r` flags of `[suites] unit` and `browser` in dev/factory.toml. Check that `fac.failed_tests` and `queue.nowhere` (dev/bin/queue.py:198-213) still read the same lines.
- After a green landing (dev/bin/queue.py, next to `gap.merged` at :842), `flakes.green(logs)` in dev/bin/flakes.py takes each item in `seen` that is not quarantined, at most 50 (lesson 4, said on stderr when hit). It reads each test's outcome from the green run's unit and browser logs with `fac.outcomes` (dev/bin/fac.py:582-588).
  - pass: `green_passes` is raised by one, written as a patch that tests the value read.
  - unknown (not collected, deselected): no change.
  - At `[gates] flake_fixed_after` (default 5, ceiling 50), `flake.fixed` is written with `fixed_by: green-runs` and `fixed_on` (the merged sha).
- Every `flake.seen` through `flakes.say` sets `green_passes: 0`, so the count is consecutive. Runs are counted in queue order, which is serial under the queue's lock (by seq, never by time: lesson 2).
- A failure here never fails or delays the landing.

## Definition of done

1. The queue's unit and browser logs carry a PASSED line per test.
2. N consecutive green runs that each name the test PASSED fix it.
3. A `flake.seen` between them restarts the count.
4. A test absent from the log never counts.
5. dev/README.md says how a flake leaves `seen`.

## Files to touch

dev/factory.toml, dev/bin/flakes.py, dev/bin/queue.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_queue.py, tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests

- `test_a_flake_is_fixed_after_n_green_runs`
- `test_not_fixed_after_n_minus_one_with_a_seen_between`
- `test_a_test_missing_from_the_green_log_never_counts` (renamed or deleted)
- `test_the_failed_and_skip_lines_still_read_with_passed_lines_on`: `failed_tests` and `nowhere` on a `-rfEsp` log.
- `test_counting_flakes_never_fails_a_landing`: `ergostat item` raising leaves the merge landed.

## Size budget

110 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: regression-flake-fixed-by-hand
gaps.title: A person can say a flake is fixed, and the quarantine's release is one event
gaps.definition:
## Problem

Some tests no run can clear. A test that was deleted or renamed stays `seen` or `main-broken` forever, and so does every goal on those stocks. manage.py has a `flake` command that writes `flake.seen` (dev/bin/manage.py:228-233) and no way out. The quarantine's release is a bare `flake.measured` with `quarantined: false` (dev/bin/fac.py:595-598), so the record cannot tell a release from any other measurement (proposal milestone gap 2, "A person's way out" and "Release and remake").

## Change

- `manage.py flake-fixed TEST --why W`: writes `flake.fixed` from `seen` or `main-broken`, with `fixed_by` (the person, BY[0]) and `why`, and records an intervention with `intervene("flake-fixed", ...)` (dev/bin/manage.py:56). An item in neither state is refused with a message.
- fac.beside's release writes `flake.released` (`quarantined: false`, `released_at`) instead of `flake.measured`. It is declared on the kind as a no-state event in its comment. `quarantined` folds as before.
- dev/README.md "Record an intervention" (dev/README.md:684) lists the command.

## Definition of done

1. `flake-fixed` moves an item from either state to `fixed` and records one intervention.
2. It refuses an unknown test or one already `fixed`.
3. A release is `flake.released`, and the item's `quarantined` is false after it.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/manage.py, dev/bin/fac.py, ergostat.yaml (comment), dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests

- `test_flake_fixed_by_hand_from_main_broken_and_seen`
- `test_flake_fixed_refuses_an_unknown_test`
- `test_a_release_is_one_event` (the beside test updated: `flake.released`, not `flake.measured`)

## Size budget

50 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: regression-flake-rate-counts-excused
gaps.title: flake-rate counts the queue's excused flakes, and has no value with no runs
gaps.definition:
## Problem

`flake-rate` reads only the gaps' `retries` over their `queue_attempts` (dev/bin/measure.py:174-176). Only triage writes `retries` (dev/bin/triage.py:77). A red run the queue itself excuses as a flake (dev/bin/queue.py:235-244) writes `flake.seen` and lands with `excused` in its `suites_queue`, but counts nowhere, so the goal `flakes-rare` (dev/model/measures.yaml:115-119) undercounts. With no runs it reads 0.0 (dev/bin/measure.py:176), which fails open (lesson 3; proposal milestone gap 3).

## Change

`flake-rate` = (triage retries in the window + queue runs in the window whose landed gaps carry `suites_queue.excused`, each run once by `batch_id`) / the queue runs in the window (distinct `run` in `queue_runs`, as merges-per-hour counts them at dev/bin/measure.py:160-164). A window with no queue runs exits 1 with no value. The docstring moves `flake-rate` into the list with no value, and the auxiliary's description in dev/model/measures.yaml says it counts both.

## Definition of done

1. An excused run raises the rate. A run excused for a batch of three counts once.
2. No runs in the window gives no value (exit 1), never 0.0.
3. Triage retries count as before.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/measure.py, dev/model/measures.yaml, tests/test_factory_measure_runs.py.

## Acceptance tests

- `test_a_run_excused_in_the_queue_moves_flake_rate`
- `test_an_excused_batch_counts_once`
- `test_flake_rate_with_no_runs_has_no_value`

30 net lines outside tests/.

gaps.name: regression-escapes-from-reverts
gaps.title: A revert on main is recorded as an escape of the gap it reverts, and escapes-found gets a sensor
gaps.definition:
## Problem

The stock `escapes` counts reverted merges, but `gap.reverted` is entered only by hand (ergostat.yaml:153-154, dev/README.md "Record an intervention"). Its inflow `escapes-found` has no sensor (dev/model/pools.yaml:66-69). A revert commit on main is therefore invisible unless someone records it (proposal section 6c and milestone gap 4).

## Change

- In `upgrade.py watch` (the block `main-watch`, dev/model/landing.yaml:358-364, dev/bin/upgrade.py:24-41), a new step `escapes.watch()` in a new module dev/bin/escapes.py walks `git rev-list --first-parent` from the last commit it read (run/escapes.json) to the pushed main. It reads at most 200 commits and says so when it hits that limit (lesson 4). It looks for `This reverts commit <sha>`.
- The reverted commit is matched to a merged gap. Either the commit is the gap's `main_sha`, or its second parent is the gap's `reviewed_head` (a `--no-ff` merge of exactly the reviewed commit, dev/bin/queue.py:4-5 and :40-41). A match writes `gap.reverted` on that gap with `reverted: true`, `revert_sha` and `reverted_at`.
- No match writes `intervention.recorded` as `intervention/reverted-<sha12>` with class `reverted-unmatched`. dev/bin/risk.py counts that class as an escape at the pool size of its time, as it does an unmatched `main-broken` (dev/bin/risk.py:79-88).
- Item ids and `revert_sha` make a second read a no-op. An unreadable mark file rescans the last 200 commits.
- `escapes-found` gets `sensor: {run: python3 dev/bin/pools.py read escapes-day, ...}`: escapes found in the last 24 hours, by `reverted_at` or `recorded_at`.

## Definition of done

1. A revert of a gap's merge records `gap.reverted` on that gap once, however often main-watch runs.
2. An unmatched revert still counts in `escapes`.
3. `escapes-found` has a sensor, and `ergostat check` reports no flow without one in pools.yaml.
4. A git error stops the escape step only, never the upgrade watch (said on stderr).
5. dev/README.md says reverts are now found by main-watch.
