gaps.name: regression-guarantees-model
gaps.title: The guarantees system: main's failing tests as a stock, held at zero by main-green
gaps.definition:
## Problem

When main breaks, the model shows it only as one `main-broken` intervention among the others (dev/model/interventions.yaml:9-12). No stock counts the tests failing on main, and no goal says "main is green" (proposal section 3, F1 row). The proposal's file `dev/model/guarantees.yaml` and its system do not exist (proposal section 6a and milestone gap 5).

## Change

- ergostat.yaml: a system `guarantees` within `oversight` (next to `measures`, ergostat.yaml:55-58), `show: [stock.main-failing-tests]`.
- dev/model/guarantees.yaml (new; `defaults: {system: guarantees}`):
  - stock `main-failing-tests`, `sensor: {items: flake, state: main-broken, every: 1m}`;
  - flows `main-tests-broken` (to it, `{items: flake, entering: main-broken, over: 1d}`) and `main-tests-fixed` (from it, `{items: flake, entering: fixed, where: {fixed_by: main-mend}, over: 1d}`, equation stock / a parameter `main-repair-time`);
  - goal `main-green`: `stock: main-failing-tests`, `hold: "<= 0"`, `tolerance: 0`, `critical: true`, `on-stale: "off"`, `per: item` (docs/SPEC.md:2213-2241);
  - `loops: {main-repair: ...}` naming the balancing loop.
- Wiring: `remedy-when` (dev/model/interventions.yaml:43-50) gains `main: goal.main-green.off`. `remedy`'s `out:` gains `flow.main-tests-fixed`. The block `main-mend` (from regression-flake-main-fixed) gets `out: flow.main-tests-fixed`. The loop closes through people and an existing program. Nothing new acts on the world.
- The owner's question, asked in this gap's "Where it stopped" and not built: should `main-green` off also hold the queue (`queue-when`, dev/model/landing.yaml:309-319) for batches that do not touch the failing tests?

## Definition of done

1. The system and file exist. `ergostat check` on ergostat.yaml reports no errors and no missing feedback for `main-green`.
2. `main-repair` is drawn balancing (`check` says so).
3. A `flake.main-broken` turns `main-green` off. Its `flake.main-fixed` turns it holding again.
4. A stale reading counts as off.
5. dev/README.md has a short section "Regression guarantees" that later gaps extend.

## Files to touch

gaps.name: regression-tests-passing-goal
gaps.title: tests-passing on main as a measure, with a goal that it does not fall over ten merges
gaps.definition:
## Problem

Nothing measures how many tests main passes, so a gap that deletes or skips tests passes every gate unseen (proposal section 4, `tests-passing`). Once regression-queue-test-counts lands, each landed run records its pytest counts.

## Change

- A new module dev/bin/passing.py with two readings. `passing.py tests-passing` gives unit + browser + host `passed` of the latest landed queue run on main, chosen by main's first-parent seq (`git rev-list --count --first-parent`, as dev/bin/measure.py:360-377 does), never by time (lesson 2). `passing.py tests-passing-change` gives the latest less the earliest within the last 10 seqs (TREND, dev/bin/measure.py:357), each sha once (the shape of `code_change`, dev/bin/measure.py:400-420).
- `counts: unknown` on the latest run, fewer than two seqs, or no checkout gives no value (exit 1). A missing summary never counts as zero (lesson 3).
- dev/model/guarantees-passing.yaml: auxiliaries `tests-passing` and `tests-passing-change` (sensors every 30m), goal `tests-not-falling`: `>= 0`, tolerance 0, `on-stale: "off"`. It is left unserved: regression-guarantees-wired wires it. Its missing-feedback finding is expected until then.

## Definition of done

1. Both readings come from the recorded counts, by seq, each sha once.
2. Unknown counts give no value.
3. `ergostat check`: no errors. The only new finding is `missing-feedback@tests-not-falling`.
4. dev/README.md "Regression guarantees" lists the measure.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/passing.py (new), dev/model/guarantees-passing.yaml (new), dev/README.md, tests/test_factory_measure_runs.py.

gaps.name: regression-escape-rate-goal
gaps.title: escape-rate, escapes per merged gap, held under the owner's setpoint
gaps.definition:

It is left unserved until regression-guarantees-wired. The pool tuner is unchanged.

gaps.name: regression-flake-measures
gaps.title: Flakes open, the hours main stays broken and the hours a flake stays unfixed, with goals
gaps.definition:
## Problem

Nothing measures how long main stays broken or a flake stays unfixed, and no goal names the oldest flake (proposal section 3, the "Time to repair" row, and section 4, `flakes-open`, `main-repair-hours`, `flake-fix-hours`). Once the flake states have ways out, those times exist in the record.

## Change

- dev/bin/flakes.py gains readings. Each is read from the items' moves in record order (`ergostat item ID --json`, as dev/bin/times.py and dev/bin/watch.py:92-101 read them), never by comparing stamps (lesson 2). At most 500 items; when it hits that limit it says so.
  - `main-repair-hours`: the median over 14 days, per stay, from the move into `main-broken` from another state to the move to `fixed`. A repeat break inside one stay does not restart the clock.
  - `flake-fix-hours`: the median from the move into `seen` to `fixed`.
  - Either with no ended stay in the window gives no value.
- dev/model/guarantees-flakes.yaml:
  - stock `flakes-open` (`{items: flake, state: seen}`);
  - goal `flakes-few`: `<= 3`, `per: item` (the oldest named), `on-stale: "off"`;
  - auxiliaries `main-repair-hours` and `flake-fix-hours`;
  - goal `main-repaired-fast`: `main-repair-hours <= 24`, `on-stale: "off"`;
  - flows `flakes-seen` and `flakes-fixed` with item sensors.
- Setpoints are parameters. Goals are unserved until regression-guarantees-wired.

## Definition of done

1. The repair hours run from the first break of a stay to its fix.
2. A remake starts a new stay.
3. Readings with nothing ended give no value.
4. `flakes-few` names its oldest items.
5. `ergostat check`: no errors.

## Files to touch

dev/bin/flakes.py, dev/model/guarantees-flakes.yaml (new), dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py.

gaps.name: regression-quarantine-goals
gaps.title: The quarantine as a stock: few tests, none held for long
gaps.definition:
## Problem

The quarantine is a file that only a reviewer reads. It is "added and released by hand" (tests/quarantine.txt:1-3), it holds eight tests today, and nothing says it is growing or stale (proposal section 3, F6 row, and section 4, `quarantined`).

- A new module dev/bin/held.py reads the list on the pushed main (`fac.quarantine`, dev/bin/fac.py:566-571, plus each line's `when` column) and cross-checks it with the flake items marked `quarantined`.

  - `held.py quarantine-oldest-days` gives the age of the oldest `when`.
  - A list or a date that cannot be read gives no value (lesson 3).

gaps.name: regression-gate-catches
gaps.title: How often each gate catches something, as evidence for keeping or changing it
gaps.definition:
## Problem

A gate that fails is a finding, not a measure. Nothing counts how often each gate catches something, so nobody can see a gate that never does (proposal section 3, F7/F8 row; section 4, `gate-catches`; the refactor path, CLAUDE.md:35-37).

## Change

- dev/bin/times.py already reads each gap's events incrementally (dev/bin/times.py:3-5, :132-160). Its per-gap output (`gap.timed`) gains `catches: {gate: n}`, counted from the gap's `gap.sent-back` events by `sent_back_by`, from `queue`, `triage`, `review`, `lint` and `measure-runs` (the writers found in dev/bin/queue.py, triage.py, review.py, plan.py, manage.py), and from the implementor's refusals for strays.

- dev/model/guarantees-gates.yaml: one auxiliary per listed gate, with no goal. A gate never off is not a regression: this is evidence (proposal section 6c).
- The simplifier's brief (dev/prompts/simplify.md) names each gate with no catch in 30 days as a candidate to question, never to remove unasked.

## Definition of done

1. The catches per gate equal the sent-back events of a fixture.
2. An unlisted sender is counted and named.
3. The auxiliaries exist with no goal.
4. The simplifier's brief carries the quiet gates.
5. `ergostat check`: no errors.

gaps.name: regression-lessons-recurring

gaps.definition:

gaps.name: regression-escape-learning
gaps.title: Each escape becomes an item, and the librarian is asked once for its lesson or test
gaps.definition:
## Problem

An escape (a reverted merge, main broken after a merge, or a gap named as a cause) only lowers the pools (dev/model/pools.yaml:113-121). Nothing learns from it: no lesson is asked for and no test is added (proposal section 4, `escapes-rare` loop; milestone gap 6).

## Change

- A kind `escape` (`escape/<gap>`, states `found`, `learned`, `dismissed`) in ergostat.yaml.
- `librarian.py escapes` (scheduled, every 30m) reads the escaped gaps from `risk.evidence` (dev/bin/risk.py:62-102, refactored to also return the blamed ids). For each one without an item it writes `escape.found` with the cause (reverted, broke_main or caused_by, and the evidence), at most 10 a run.
- A block `escape-librarian` takes `escape` at `found` under a lease (`takes:`, pool 1, `lease: {attempts: 2}`), so each escape gets one step (lesson 1). The step is one small AI call with the librarian prompt and the gap's definition, diff stat and cause. It either proposes a lesson through the existing gated `knowledge-change` (`propose`, dev/bin/librarian.py:30-32) or requests a gap that adds the missing test (`gap.requested`, source `escape`). Then it writes `escape.learned` with what it asked. A step that cannot decide writes `escape.dismissed` with why.
- dev/model/guarantees-escapes.yaml gains the stock `escapes-unlearned` (`{items: escape, state: found}`) and `loops: {escape-learning: ...}`.

## Definition of done

1. An escape makes one item, however often the scan runs.
2. Each item gets one librarian step.
3. Its outcome is a gated proposal or a requested gap, never a direct edit.
4. It runs within the day's AI cap (`fac.may_spend`).
5. `ergostat check`: no errors.

## Files to touch

ergostat.yaml, dev/bin/librarian.py, dev/bin/risk.py, dev/model/guarantees-escapes.yaml, dev/model/knowledge.yaml (the block), dev/prompts/librarian.md, tests/test_factory_knowledge.py.

gaps.name: regression-guarantees-wired
gaps.title: Every regression goal reaches the coordinator through one block, and every loop is named
gaps.definition:
## Problem

The measure gaps land their goals unserved, each one missing feedback (docs/SPEC.md:2232), on purpose, so parallel gaps never edit the same lines. Until something serves them, a broken guarantee shows only as a `check` finding (proposal section 6a, point 4).

gaps.name: regression-fixes-hold-goal
gaps.title: The repair template's goal that no fix regressed in the last 14 days, and the stock in SPEC's parts table
gaps.definition:
## Problem

The repair template has the stock `regressed-fixes` and the flows `fixes-regressed` and `fixes-reverted` (ergostat/library/templates/repair/template.yaml:49, :63-64). Its only goals are `no-open-failures` and `fixes-answered` (template.yaml:66-67), so a fix that regressed breaks no goal. A goal on the stock itself could never recover: a denied `revert-fix` leaves the failure `regressed` for good (docs/SPEC.md:6710). SPEC's parts table leaves the stock out (docs/SPEC.md:6723). (Proposal section 3, the U3 row; milestone gap 7.)

## Change

- template.yaml: an auxiliary `fixes-regressed-recent`, `sensor: {items: ergostat.failure, entering: regressed, over: 14d}`, `driven-by: +flow.fixes-regressed`, and a goal `fixes-hold`: `<= 0`, `tolerance: 0`, `on-stale: "off"`. It recovers when a window passes with no new regression. It is served by the existing revert ask: each regressed fix already has its revert asked as a gated action (docs/SPEC.md:6278-6293 area, the repair section). If `check` finds no block serving it, the template's person approver block reads it.
- SPEC section 12r: the parts table lists `regressed-fixes`, `fixes-regressed-recent` and `fixes-hold`, and says why the goal is on the window, not the stock.

## Definition of done

1. A model using `repair` gets `fixes-hold`. A regressed fix turns it off. It holds again after a window with none.
2. `ergostat check` on a model using the template reports no errors and no missing feedback for it.
3. The SPEC table matches the template.

## Files to touch

ergostat/library/templates/repair/template.yaml, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_repair_verify.py.

- `test_a_regressed_fix_turns_fixes_hold_off`

gaps.name: regression-template
gaps.title: A library template, regressions, that gives a user's model passing counts, escapes and regressed fixes
gaps.definition:
## Problem

Ergostat adds nothing of its own accord (CLAUDE.md:52-53), so a user gets regression guarantees only by asking. There is no template to ask for (proposal section 6b; milestone gap 7).

## Change

A template ergostat/library/templates/regressions/template.yaml, used as `uses: {regressions: {use: regressions, with: {...}}}` (the way the factory uses `interventions`):
- **Passing counts**: an auxiliary `tests-failing` whose sensor runs the model's declared `claims: tests` command (docs/SPEC.md:5236) on a schedule (`every` parameter) through a small reader, `python -m ergostat.regressions counts`. The reader gets a pytest-style summary parser in ergostat/regressions.py. A run that cannot be read, or has no summary, gives no value. Goal `tests-green`: `<= 0`, `on-stale: "off"`.
- **Escapes**: an auxiliary on `builtin: ergostat.trust.contradicted@${block}` (docs/SPEC.md:5299-5309), goal `claims-kept` `<= ${escape-share}`.

notes:
Notes: <workdir>/design/plan/wave2-merge-pipeline.md. 13 gaps in four tracks; the four tracks can start at once. Already filed, so not proposed again: bisect-tests-main-itself and queue-runs-what-its-container-skips. Two of my gaps depend on bisect-tests-main-itself, because they edit land() or picks() after it.

Evidence from the live factory's record (2026-11-22):
(a) GAPS.md. The union merge from gaps-md-no-collisions turned textual conflicts into splices. Three reviewer send-backs today cite lesson-7 GAPS.md splices. Two queue failures came from tests that pin GAPS.md text (tests/test_gaps_doc.py, tests/test_item_search_gaps.py). The cause is house-rules.md:33-34, together with umbrella entries that every sub-gap appends to.
(b) Serial bisect. The cost is one 9-minute full run per failing merge, not the 1-minute named runs. operating-states-20261122T094631Z made 23 suite runs from 09:46 to 11:01.
(c) Stacked branches. Dependents wait for the merge because precedence is finish-to-start (building.yaml:209, ergostat.yaml:115/291), and agents.clone always branches from main.
(d) Browser trigger. browser and rerun run -q -rs (factory.toml:170/180), so they print no FAILED lines. Every browser red in the record is anonymous: never excused, never bisected by name, and triage sends it to fix.

Design choices:
- (a) Each entry moves into its gap's record as an `## Entry` section. Sub-gaps contribute `done:` lines by `entry-of:`. The queue regenerates GAPS.md on the landed head, and a branch that edits GAPS.md is refused.
- (b) Speculation runs only the cheap checks (the named tests and ruff), on every prefix at once, each in its own worktree and container, then one full run on the survivors.
- (c) A generic relation option `starts_at`. A stacked gap brings its base into its own batch, below it. A failed base gives its descendants back uncounted. Merge-forward never rebases or squashes. stacks-turned-on is the only gap that switches stacking on.
- (d) The daily main browser run comes before the path trigger, which skips browser on batches that touch none of its paths.

Not covered: speculation over full suites (not enough CPUs), and restacking when a base parks (the descendant waits, as today).

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-gaps-entries-in-records
gaps.title: A GAPS.md entry lives in its gap's record, and docs/GAPS.md is rendered from the records
gaps.definition:
## Problem
One shared file is edited by nearly every branch. dev/knowledge/house-rules.md:33-34 tells each gap to keep GAPS current. Umbrella entries collect one "done on X" sentence from each sub-gap: the Remote systems entry, docs/GAPS.md:9-45, holds about ten. The union merge (docs/.gitattributes, from gaps-md-no-collisions) removed textual conflicts but splices paragraphs instead. On 2026-11-22 three reviewer send-backs cite lesson-7 GAPS.md splices: relative-gain-array at 06:28, remote-items-record at 06:30 and remote-process-lines at 06:57. Fix rounds were spent resolving splices as well (commit ec398175). This gap builds the format and the renderer only. Nothing reads them yet.

## Change
A new module, dev/bin/gapsdoc.py:
- parse(record_text) returns the record's `## Entry` section. It holds `section: <GAPS section title>`, optionally `entry-of: <branch>` and `done: YYYY-MM-DD <sentence>` lines, and the entry's bullet text as it appears in GAPS.md today.
- render(records, head) returns the text of docs/GAPS.md. It takes the records {branch: text} and the head (the preamble and the section order). Within a section, entries come in their `order:` value, then by title. A record with `entry-of: B` adds its done sentences as indented `*Done*` lines under B's entry, in date order, so no two branches edit one paragraph. A record with no Entry renders nothing.
- split(gaps_md_text) is the inverse. For each top-level entry of today's GAPS.md it returns {branch: entry section} (branch = fac.slug(slug(title, 60), 32), as intake.py:225 assigns it), plus the head. The head goes to dev/records/GAPS-head.md.
- A CLI: `python3 dev/bin/gapsdoc.py render [--check]` and `python3 dev/bin/gapsdoc.py split --dry-run`.
No record is written and no reader changes in this gap.

## Definition of done
1. render(split(text)) == text for today's docs/GAPS.md, line for line, apart from trailing whitespace. Any normalisation is listed in the module docstring.
2. Two records with `entry-of` the same umbrella, edited on two branches, merge with no conflict. The rendered umbrella holds both done lines, each once.
3. A record with a malformed Entry (no `section:`, or a section not in the head) is reported by name, never skipped silently (lesson-3). `render --check` exits 1 and names it.
4. A branch named twice (two entries that slug to one branch) is reported, never resolved by picking one.
5. The module docstring states the Entry shape. dev/prompts/definition.md shows it in one short example.

## Files to touch
dev/bin/gapsdoc.py (new), dev/prompts/definition.md, tests/test_gapsdoc.py (new).

## Acceptance tests
- tests/test_gapsdoc.py::test_split_then_render_gives_todays_gaps_md

## Change
Run `gapsdoc.py split` once and commit its output: each entry becomes the `## Entry` section of dev/records/<branch>.md. It is appended to an existing record, never overwriting one. The head goes to dev/records/GAPS-head.md. Switch every reader to gapsdoc.parse over main's dev/records/ (git ls-tree and git show on the base, as they read GAPS.md now). twice() is retired, since one file per entry cannot list an entry twice, and the branch collision report from gapsdoc stands in its place. A record holding only an Entry is not a definition of done:
- intake.definition() and brief.definition_text take a record as a definition only when it has a `## Definition of done` section;
- implement.definition_first appends the definition to such a record rather than skipping it (implement.py:49).
The two pinning tests move to fixture records.

2. deps.py gives the same links and sources from records as from the GAPS.md they were split from. Each source names the record file and line.
3. The brief's and planner's entry text is the record's Entry, rendered. The fallback `(missing: ...)` names dev/records/.
4. An Entry-only record never moves a gap to ready.
5. No test under tests/ reads docs/GAPS.md. A test checks this.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-gaps-md-regenerated-on-land
gaps.title: The merge queue regenerates docs/GAPS.md on each landed head, and no branch edits it
gaps.definition:
## Problem
Once the readers use dev/records/, docs/GAPS.md is still what people read, and it goes stale unless something writes it. House-rules.md:33-34 and the briefs still tell sessions to keep GAPS current, so branches would keep editing the shared file. The union rule in docs/.gitattributes keeps hiding the splices.

## Change
- queue.py: after land() and before ask() (queue.py:860-861), run gapsdoc.render on the landed head. When the result differs from docs/GAPS.md, commit it on the checkout's main as `docs/GAPS.md from the records` with the trailer. That commit is the one pushed. It changes docs/GAPS.md alone, and no test reads that file (the readers gap guarantees it). A render that fails (a malformed record) lands the batch without the commit and says why on the run (`gaps_md: why`). It never blocks a merge.
- implement.py: before the suites, next to strays (implement.py:228-231), a branch whose diff against main touches docs/GAPS.md is refused back to its next round with a brief: `edit the Entry in dev/records/<branch>.md; docs/GAPS.md is generated`. The refusal is uncounted, as strays are.
- Remove `GAPS.md merge=union` from docs/.gitattributes.
- Rewrite house-rules.md:33-34 to say: keep SPEC and the agent guide current; the gap's state goes in its record's Entry.

## Definition of done
1. A batch of two gaps whose records change two sub-entries of one umbrella lands, and the pushed head's docs/GAPS.md shows both.
2. A batch whose records render what main has already makes no extra commit.
3. A malformed record lands the batch and says gaps_md on the run. Main's docs/GAPS.md is left as it was.
4. A branch editing docs/GAPS.md is refused before its suites, with the brief above, uncounted.
5. The queue's docstring (item 6) and dev/README.md (Batches) say so.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-prefix-runs-in-parallel
gaps.title: The queue can run one check on every prefix of a batch at once, each in its own worktree and container
gaps.definition:
## Problem
The queue tests one tree at a time, its checkout (queue.py:91-169). Bisecting a batch is therefore serial: queue.py:705-709 halves the batch one step at a time and runs once per step. On 2026-11-22, operating-states-20261122T094631Z made 23 suite runs from 09:46 to 11:01. Four of them were full runs of about 9 minutes, and twelve were named runs of about 1 minute, one after another (run/queue/ log times). agents.queued (agents.py:434-450) already supports a worktree as the work, so trees can be tested side by side.

## Change
A new module, dev/bin/prefixes.py. Never name it after a stdlib module (queue.py:59). It provides run_all(cfg, repo, heads, check, tag, logs, most). For each commit in heads, it makes a detached worktree under run/queue-prefix/<tag>-<i>, named by this code and removed by name afterwards. Then it runs check(i, worktree) for each, at most `most` at a time, in threads. check is fac.suite with box "queue" for a given suite (rerun with tests, or ruff). The result per prefix is pass, fail or unknown, with its log. A stop (fac.stop_suites, SIGTERM) kills every container by name and removes every worktree it made. A worktree left by a SIGKILLed run is removed at the next run's start, under the queue's lock. `[suites] prefix_most` (default 4, at most 8) caps concurrency. `[agents]` gives each prefix container `prefix_cpus` CPUs (default 1.5), within queue_cpuset.

## Definition of done
1. run_all on 5 heads returns 5 results in heads' order, each read from its own log. A run that does not start is unknown, never pass (lesson-3).
2. At most prefix_most checks run at once.
3. Stopping a run part way leaves no container (by name) and no worktree under run/queue-prefix/.
4. A worktree from a killed run is removed at the next start, and only those under run/queue-prefix/ that match the run-tag pattern (deletes by allowlist).
5. The settings are in dev/factory.toml with comments. Values out of bounds are refused, with the reason given.

## Files to touch
dev/bin/prefixes.py (new), dev/bin/agents.py (the per-prefix CPU limit), dev/factory.toml, tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests
- tests/test_factory.py::test_prefix_runs_return_one_result_per_head_in_order

- tests/test_factory.py::test_a_stopped_prefix_run_leaves_no_worktree_or_container
- tests/test_factory.py::test_a_prefix_run_that_did_not_start_is_unknown

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-bisect-in-parallel-rounds
gaps.title: A red batch finds every failing merge in parallel rounds of its named tests, then lands on one full run
gaps.definition:
## Problem
After finding a failing merge, land() starts a new full run on the rest (queue.py:718-722), so each failing merge costs a full run of about 9 to 13 minutes. Two batches on 2026-11-22 show the pattern:
- operating-states-20261122T094631Z: full, 3 named, full, 3 named, ... five full runs, 75 minutes;
- queue-runs-what-its-container-skips-20261122T083445Z: 08:34 to 09:46.
In both, the named tests decided each step. A ruff failure names no test, so it bisects with full runs of every suite (queue.py:698).

## Change
In land(), a red run that named tests which fail alone on the red tree (and that bisect-tests-main-itself does not hand to main) is bisected in rounds:
1. Run the named tests on every prefix at once (prefixes.run_all).
2. The first failing prefix's last merge is the failing merge. Give it to triage as now (queue-failed, pre, findings). The stacked descendants it gives back are given back with it (stacks-land-bottom-up).
3. Rebuild the survivors' heads without it, and go back to step 1 until the named tests pass on the whole survivor tree.
4. Run the full suites once on the survivors. Green lands them. Red with new names starts again.
A ruff failure is bisected the same way with ruff per prefix. A prefix that cannot tell (unknown) falls back to today's serial step for that round. The time allowance (Late) is checked before each round. Each run records batch_rounds and prefix_runs on suites_queue.

## Definition of done
1. A batch of 8 with one failing merge makes: one full run, one named run on the red tree, the main check, one parallel round, and one full run on the 7. The 7 land.
2. A batch of 8 with two independent failing merges is found in two rounds, with one final full run.
3. A ruff failure in merge 5 of 8 is found in one ruff round.
4. An unknown prefix result never counts as a pass: that round goes serial.
5. Past the allowance, only a prefix a full green run proved lands, as now.
6. The queue docstring (item 6) and dev/README.md (Batches) give the cost per failing merge.

## Files to touch
dev/bin/queue.py, dev/README.md, tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests
- tests/test_factory.py::test_one_failing_merge_of_eight_costs_one_parallel_round_and_one_full_run
- tests/test_factory.py::test_two_failing_merges_take_two_rounds_and_one_full_run
- tests/test_factory.py::test_a_ruff_failure_is_found_in_one_round
- tests/test_factory.py::test_an_unknown_prefix_result_falls_back_to_serial

## Risks
- A test that fails only from an interaction of two merges fails on a prefix that holds both. The later merge is blamed, as serial bisect does today. Say so in the docstring.

## Size budget
120 net lines in dev/bin.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-relation-starts-at
gaps.title: A precedence relation may name the target states at which a dependent may start
gaps.definition:
## Problem
Precedence is finish-to-start only. A dependent is unblocked once each target is in a finished state (ergostat/precedence.py:93-105; ergostat/leases/ready.py:75-84). The factory's gaps wait for a dependency to be reviewed, queued, merged and pushed before they start (ergostat.yaml:115, 291; dev/model/building.yaml:209), though work could start from an approved branch. A team modelled in ergostat has the same need (a ticket that can start once another is in review). This gap is the engine part only. The factory does not use it yet.

## Change
A relation's map form takes `starts_at: [STATE, ...]`, states of the target kind (ergostat/spec/relations.py REL_KEYS, the Relation IR). A target in one of those states does not block for `takes: {unblocked: true}` or for precedence status: the item is `unblocked`, not `blocked`. The CPM forward pass and the schedule stay finish-to-start, which is conservative, and the docstring and SPEC say so. check refuses:
- a state the target kind lacks;
- starts_at on a relation that is not precedence;
- a finished or paused state named in starts_at (meaningless).
The item index and the Items API expose starts_at with the relation.

## Definition of done
1. `depends_on: {kind: gap, starts_at: [approved]}`: a gap whose only dependency is approved is taken by an `unblocked: true` block. With the dependency in fix, it is not.
2. Precedence status says unblocked for it. The critical path still waits for the dependency's finish.
3. check gives one finding for each refusal above, with a stated code.
4. SPEC §5a (Relations) and §9.5 (takes) say what starts_at does and does not change.
5. The schema (schema/ergostat.schema.json) knows the key.

## Files to touch
ergostat/spec/relations.py, ergostat/spec/ir.py, ergostat/precedence.py, ergostat/leases/ready.py (if the waiting list is built there), schema/ergostat.schema.json, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_relations.py, tests/test_precedence.py.

## Acceptance tests

## Size budget
90 net lines.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacked-gap-builds-on-its-base
gaps.title: A gap whose dependencies are approved is built on their reviewed branches, not on main
gaps.definition:
## Problem
agents.clone always starts a new branch from origin/main (agents.py:282-296). implement.py measures and merges against main: base_sha at implement.py:200, merge_main at 202, finish's also at 227, strays at 228, net_lines at 244, and onmain.check at 238. So a gap cannot start until each gap it depends on has merged. This gap makes the implementor able to build on a base. It stays inert until stacks-turned-on lets such a gap be taken.

## Change
fac.stack_base(cfg, gap) returns, for a gap whose unfinished dependencies are each in approved, queued or push-pending, their reviewed heads ({gap, sha}, rank order). For any other gap it returns none. implement.py, when there are bases:
- clones as now, then merges each base's reviewed head into the branch (`--no-ff`, by this program, like merge_main). Never a rebase or a squash.
- records `stacked_on: [{gap, sha}]` on gap.started and gap.built.
- uses, as the base for strays, net_lines, the check findings and onmain's main comparison, the merge of main and every base (a commit in the drop under refs/stack/<branch>, made by this program).
- has finish hold each base sha as well as main.
Bases that conflict with each other give the gap back uncounted, with the files named and after 30m. A base whose reviewed head is no longer its branch's tip waits for the merge-forward and is given back uncounted.

## Definition of done
1. A gap with one approved dependency starts from that dependency's reviewed head merged with main. Its net_lines and strays count only its own commits.
2. With two approved dependencies, both are merged in rank order. If they conflict with each other, the gap is given back uncounted, naming the files.
3. stacked_on is on the item after gap.built, with each base's sha.
4. finish refuses a head that no longer holds a base's sha.
5. A gap with no unfinished dependency builds exactly as today: a test pins it.
6. implement.py's docstring step 1 says so.

## Files to touch
dev/bin/fac.py, dev/bin/implement.py, dev/bin/agents.py (finish's held shas), tests/test_factory.py.

## Acceptance tests
- tests/test_factory.py::test_a_stacked_gap_starts_from_its_bases_reviewed_head
- tests/test_factory.py::test_a_stacked_gaps_net_lines_count_only_its_own_commits
- tests/test_factory.py::test_two_bases_that_conflict_give_the_gap_back_uncounted

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacks-land-bottom-up
gaps.title: The merge queue lands a stacked gap only with or after its base, and never without it
gaps.definition:
## Problem
A stacked branch holds its base's reviewed commits. picks() (queue.py:505-558) and land() (queue.py:635-729) see only each gap's reviewed commit. Taken alone, a stacked gap would land its base's work under its own name, and the base would later merge as nothing. In a red batch, the merges after a failing one are merged again onto the green prefix (queue.py:718-722). A descendant of the failing merge would then bring the failing commit back. This gap makes the queue safe for stacked gaps. It reads the field `stacked_on: [{gap, sha}]` that the implementor writes.

## Change
- picks(): a gap whose stacked_on names a gap not merged on main (its sha not an ancestor of pre) brings that base in below it, bottom-up (recursively). The base must be approved and held by no run. A base that is not approved, or a stack that does not fit the batch cap n with the run's own gap, gives the run's own gap back uncounted (after 10m) with the reason. It is never counted towards EMPTY_MOST (queue.py:561-580). A stacked batch-mate whose base cannot come along is skipped and stays approved.
- land(): when a merge is blamed (queue-failed), every later merge in the batch whose stacked_on reaches it (at any depth) is given back to approved uncounted. It is never merged again onto the green prefix.

## Definition of done
1. Base A and stacked B, both approved: a run on B tests and lands A, then B, in that order, in one batch.
2. B whose base A is in fix is given back uncounted, with the reason. Its empty_batches is unchanged.
3. A batch where A fails: B is given back to approved, and the green prefix lands without A's or B's commits (checked by the pushed tree).
4. A stack of 3 with a batch cap of 2 gives the run's own gap back uncounted, and the bottom base lands in its own run.
5. A batch with no stacked gap behaves exactly as today: a test pins it.
6. The queue's docstring (step 3, item 6) says so.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-stacks-merged-forward
gaps.title: When a stacked gap's base moves, the new base is merged forward into it; a conflict goes back to its implementor
gaps.definition:
## Problem
A base can change after its descendant started. It may go back to fix and be approved at a new head, or triage may send it back and a fix round add commits. The descendant still holds the old reviewed sha. The queue then refuses it, or (stacks-land-bottom-up) brings in a base whose reviewed head the descendant does not hold. Nothing carries the base's new commits forward. Rebasing or squashing would discard the review history, so the owner's direction is to merge them forward.

## Change
A new program, dev/bin/stack.py, run as a block stack-forward in dev/model/building.yaml (every 5m, commanded by a sensor counting stale stacks). For each gap with stacked_on whose base's reviewed head has moved and is approved again (or whose base has landed, when there is nothing to do but update stacked_on):
- if the gap is leased, building or in review, skip it. The next implementor round merges the base itself.
- otherwise merge the new base head into the gap's branch in a scratch clone of the drop, `--no-ff`, by the factory (never a rebase or a squash), and move the drop's branch from its old tip only (update-ref old value).
- clean, on an approved gap: record the new reviewed_head with `reviewed_by: stack-forward` and the new stacked_on. The merge brings only reviewed commits, and the queue tests the result.
- clean, on a built or fix gap: move the branch, and leave the next round or review to run.
- conflict: abort and send the gap back to fix with the files (`stack_conflict`), uncounted as a failed gate. implement.py's next round merges the base again and hands the conflict to the session (its conflict brief, implement.py:147-151).
Descendants are processed bottom-up, so a stack of three moves in one pass.

## Definition of done
1. Base A re-approved at a new head: an approved descendant B gets a merge commit of A's new head, keeps approved, and its reviewed_head and stacked_on are updated.
2. A conflicting merge-forward sends B to fix with the files and is not counted as a failed gate.
3. A leased or in-review descendant is never touched.
4. A stack of three moves forward in one pass, bottom-up.
5. A drop branch that moved during the merge is refused, and theirs is kept.
6. The block and its sensor are in the model. `ergostat check` adds no finding.

## Problem
dev/factory.toml:170 runs the browser suite with `-q -rs`, and :180 runs the rerun with `-q -rs`. `-r` replaces pytest's default `fE`, so no FAILED or ERROR line is printed, and fac.failed_tests (dev/bin/fac.py:556-561) finds none. As a result:
- it is never excused as a flake (queue.py:217-222);
- it is bisected with full runs of every suite (queue.py:698);
- triage says "named no test" and sends it to fix (triage.py:60).

## Change
`browser` and `rerun` use `-rfEs`, with a comment like the unit suite's. Add a test that each suite command in dev/factory.toml that fac.failed_tests reads (unit, host, build, browser, rerun, alone) keeps f and E in its -r, or has no -r at all.

## Definition of done
1. A browser run with a failing test yields that test from fac.failed_tests.
2. queue.suites's skip count (`^SKIPPED`, queue.py:111) and nowhere() still read the same skips.
3. The config test fails if a later edit drops f or E.

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-browser-daily-on-main
gaps.title: Once a day the browser suite runs on main; a flake is recorded, a real failure names its tests and suspects
gaps.definition:
## Problem
The owner wants the browser suite run on a trigger rather than in every batch. A batch-only trigger (merge-pipeline-browser-only-on-its-paths) needs a safety net for changes outside those paths that still break a page, such as a model loader change that alters what a diagram draws. Nothing runs the browser suite on main by itself today. Each batch's run is the only one (queue.py:156).

## Change
A new program, dev/bin/browserday.py, run as a block browser-daily in dev/model/landing.yaml (every: 24h). It works under the queue's lock (fac.queue_lock), so it never overlaps a batch, after fac.wait_quiet. It runs the browser suite (box "queue", quarantine from main) in a detached worktree at origin/main, made and removed by name.
- Green: write {sha, at} to run/browser-daily.json.
- Red: rerun each named test alone twice (the named() shape, `-rA`). A test that passes both times is flake.seen (suite browser, run, log). The others form an intervention of class queue naming the tests, main's sha, and the first-parent merges since the last green sha (git log --first-parent) as suspects. pipeline-watch already turns a queue intervention into a situation.
- No names (a crash, a skip): an intervention with the tail.
A sensor browser-main-green (1, 0, or no reading when the file cannot be read: lesson-3) and a goal on it make the result visible on the Dynamics diagram. No new page.

## Definition of done
1. A green run records the sha. A run the next day with no merge between still runs (it tests main, not changes).
2. A failure that passes alone twice is a flake, and no intervention is raised.
3. A real failure raises one intervention naming the tests, the sha and the suspect merges since the last green.
4. The run holds the queue's lock. A batch waiting for the lock starts after it.
5. Its worktree and containers are removed on every way out.
6. `ergostat check` adds no finding. dev/README.md says what the daily run does.

## Files to touch

gaps.name: merge-pipeline-browser-only-on-its-paths
gaps.title: A batch runs the browser suite only when it touches the pages, the examples, the layout fixtures or the browser tests
gaps.definition:
## Problem
Every queue run, including each bisect step, runs the four browser files beside the unit suite (queue.py:156; factory.toml:170). That is about 9-10 minutes of 4 CPUs per run (run/queue/*-browser.txt on 2026-11-22). Most batches change no page: of the 30 queue send-backs on 2026-11-22, the conflicting files were almost all under ergostat/spec, ergostat/remote, dev/bin and docs. With the daily main run in place, the owner's direction is to run the browser suite in a batch only when the batch touches what it tests.

## Change
`[suites] browser_paths` in dev/factory.toml lists globs, by default ergostat/web/**, examples/**, tests/fixtures/layout_known.json, tests/fixtures/diagram_sizes.json, tests/layout_*, and the four browser test files. queue.suites runs the browser step only when `git diff --name-only pre HEAD` matches one of them. Otherwise the run records `browser: {not_run: "no browser path changed"}` on suites_queue. rest() (queue.py:230-232) and excused() treat a suite that was not run as finished, never as stopped. An empty list runs browser every time, as today. Bisect sub-runs of a batch use the batch's decision.

## Definition of done
1. A batch touching only dev/bin runs no browser step and records not_run.
2. A batch touching ergostat/web/ runs it, as today.
3. A red unit run in a batch without browser paths never runs browser for rest().
4. `browser_paths = []` runs browser in every batch.
5. The queue's docstring (step 5) and dev/README.md say so, and name the daily main run as the net.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-walk-and-demo-scripts
gaps.title: Two scripts let a session start a demo and walk it in Chromium: demo_up.py and walk.py
gaps.definition:
Problem: no factory session can look at a running demo. The design review's walker lives outside the repository (the design folder's browse.py), and the only demo runner, scripts/demo_check.py:150-187 (fresh_copy, OFFLINE), is a whole check that cannot be asked for one demo left running. Sessions run only allowlisted commands (dev/bin/agents.py:38-46), so without a named script no implementor, designer or researcher can open a page. Chromium is already in the image (Dockerfile: playwright==1.63.0, /opt/ms-playwright; tests/test_agents.py:25).

Change: add scripts/demo_up.py, which uses demo_check's fresh_copy and OFFLINE. `demo_up.py start DEMO [--port N]` copies examples/DEMO to a new folder under /tmp, runs it with `python -m ergostat -C COPY run --port N`, waits up to 90 s for its web to answer, and prints one JSON line {demo, url, copy, log}. `demo_up.py stop DEMO` stops it. A demo name must be a folder of examples/ that holds an ergostat.yaml; anything else is refused. Also add scripts/walk.py, the design review's walker brought in with tests. It reads a JSON list of steps (goto, size, dark, wait, click, hover, fill, press, scroll, shot, text) and runs them in one Chromium page, 1440x900 by default. It launches Chromium with no proxy for 127.0.0.1 and localhost, and with HTTPS_PROXY as Chromium's proxy for any other host when that is set. A step that fails is printed and the walk goes on. 4. walk.py passes no proxy for loopback URLs and HTTPS_PROXY for others (unit-tested on the launch arguments).

- A URL source must appear in the session's own tool calls: WebFetch urls, WebSearch result urls, or the walker's goto. These are read from the session item's tool_calls (dev/bin/sessions.py), which are folded when the session ends.
- An answer with at least one checked source is answered, with `sources_checked` (the checked ones) and `sources_unchecked` (the rest, with why).
- An answer with none says research.unsourced (a new state, unsourced), and the question is asked again once, with the reason in the brief. The second unsourced answer is research.dead (a new state, dead, which plan.py:304 and manage.py:295 already read).
- In the model: a flow research-unsourced, and research-answered counts only answered.

Definition of done:
1. A report citing an existing file and line is answered, with that source in sources_checked.
2. A report citing only a file that is missing, or a line past the end, is unsourced, and the item says which and why.
3. A URL the session never opened is unchecked. One it fetched is checked.
4. The second unsourced answer for one question makes it dead, and a planner waiting on it plans without it (plan.py's existing dead path).
5. The stand-in researcher's answer cites a real file, so the existing tests keep passing.
6. The researcher's prompt says sources are checked and how.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-research-in-gap-briefs
gaps.title: A gap's answered research is in its implementor's, reviewer's and planner's briefs, and the coordinator can ask research for a gap
gaps.definition:
Problem: research answers are read once and lost. The planner gets the reports of its own questions while it plans (dev/bin/plan.py:312, cut at 4000 characters), and then nobody else does. knowledge.block gives the implementor and the reviewer decisions, related gaps, findings and the module map (dev/bin/knowledge.py:36-39), and no research. The reports live in the instance's run/research/ (research.py:46), which no session container can read. The proposal says so: "A planner waiting on it is given the report once and nobody reads it again" (docs/proposals/knowledge-graph.md:19). dev/bin/ask.py cannot tie a question to a gap.

Change: add a source "research" to knowledge.block, first in MORE for the implementor, reviewer and planner. It is the answered research items in the gap's `research` field and its parents' (the planner's questions), plus those whose `gap` field names the gap or a parent. Each is shown as its question, summary and report, read with research.report and cut to [knowledge] research_chars (default 6000) apiece, within the role's budget, with its id recorded as carried or dropped like any entry. ask.py gets --gap GAP, which records `gap` on the research item and refuses a gap that does not exist. A research question whose gap is building waits for nothing: it is carried by the next round's brief.

Definition of done:
1. An implementor brief for a gap whose planner asked research carries that report under "Research for this gap", and its context lists the research id.
2. A reviewer's brief carries it too.
3. An item still asked, or unsourced or dead, is not carried.
4. Over the budget, it is dropped and recorded as dropped, never cut mid-tag.
5. ask.py --gap records the gap and refuses an unknown one.
6. dev/knowledge/README.md says what briefs carry.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-findings-applied-carried
gaps.title: The knowledge queue holds findings: a sourced research answer is proposed as a finding, applied by lesson-apply and carried by area
gaps.definition:
Problem: the knowledge base holds only the house rules, the review lessons and the decisions. A `finding` entry kind exists, but such entries are "synced as items but not yet carried in briefs" (dev/knowledge/README.md:24). What research learns about the code or the world never reaches the next gap in the same area (docs/proposals/knowledge-graph.md:19). The knowledge queue (lesson items, the knowledge-change gate, lesson-apply; dev/bin/lesson.py:1-11) works, but it takes only lesson entries and "seen as" lines (lesson.py:30-40; knowledge.applied, knowledge.py:103-127). The kb-* gaps that would carry facts are parked because their facts became gaps (kb-proposals: "approval makes a gap"), which the owner refused.

Change: let lesson items take kind `finding`.
- When research.py says research.answered with at least one checked source, it proposes one: lesson/finding-<slug of the question, at most 40>-<hash6>, kind finding. Its entry is the summary plus "Source: research/<id>" and the checked sources. Its areas are the --areas given to ask.py, or for a planner's question the gap's touched packages. It is asked as knowledge-change, as the librarian does, at most one per answer, and never again for an id in any state.
- lesson-apply applies an approved finding into the record.
- knowledge.applied turns each applied finding into an entry `finding-<slug>` of kind finding with its areas.
- knowledge.block carries findings for the implementor, planner and researcher roles by the same area-word match as decisions, under "What the factory has found", recorded carried or dropped.
- `lesson.py retire` works on findings.
- In the model: the stock lessons-proposed counts findings too (description), and a stock findings-active counts the active findings.

Definition of done:
1. A checked answer proposes exactly one finding, asked through knowledge-change. An unsourced one proposes none.
2. Approved and applied, it is an entry finding-<slug> carried in the brief of a gap whose text names one of its areas, and not in one that names none.
3. A denied finding is never proposed again.
4. Retiring a finding stops it being carried.
5. No gap is made at any step.
6. dev/knowledge/README.md describes findings, and says each is approved before it lands and that private material never does.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-story-kind-and-sync
gaps.title: User stories are items: story/A1..H6 synced from docs/roadmap/stories.md, owned by the design system
gaps.definition:
Problem: the 46 stories are the measure of whether a newcomer can use ergostat, but the factory does not know they exist. They are a markdown file that the filed stories-reflect-owner-decisions brings in as docs/roadmap/stories.md. They are walked by documentation-only gaps (stories-rerun-after-owner-list, stories-rerun-after-redesigns), which go through the gap queue and its implementors. That is the wrong queue by the owner's rule of one queue per kind of work (ergostat.yaml:85-158 is the gap kind, built for code). There is no story kind, no stock of stories and no goal that says how many are possible and obvious.

Change: add an item kind `story` in ergostat.yaml.
- Ids story/<code> (a1, b2).
- States: due, obvious, possible, impossible, not-yet, retired. Events: story.listed and story.due go to due; story.obvious, story.possible, story.impossible and story.not-yet go to their states; story.retired goes to retired. done is [retired].
- Shown: section, title, audience, demo, url, done_when, baseline, walked_at, walked_sha, screenshots, gaps. A relation gaps: gap.
- Add a new dev/bin/stories.py with `sync`, a program block every 10 minutes. It parses docs/roadmap/stories.md on main: each ### heading with its As, Demo and Done-when bullets, and the demo from the URL's port through the file's Demos table. It lists new stories, writes story.changed (no state) when the text changes, and retires stories no longer in the file. A file that cannot be parsed stops it with nothing recorded.
- Add a system `design` within factory, and a new dev/model/design.yaml with stocks stories-due, stories-obvious and stories-impossible (sensors by state) and an auxiliary stories-obvious-share (obvious over all not retired). A goal stories-obvious holds the share >= 0.8 with tolerance 0.1; the 0.8 is an estimate and marked so, and the owner sets it.

Definition of done:
1. With docs/roadmap/stories.md on main, a sync lists every story with its demo, URL and done-when, and a second sync writes nothing.
2. Editing a story's text writes story.changed. Removing a story retires it.
3. A heading without a Demo line, or a demo port not in the table, refuses the sync with the heading named, and nothing is recorded.
4. The model loads (ergostat check), with the design system, its stocks and its goal.
5. dev/README.md has a short "The story queue" section.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-stories-due-after-merges
gaps.title: Stories become due again after a merge touches the page code or their demo, a few a day, failing ones first
gaps.definition:
Problem: a story is worth re-testing only when something it depends on has changed: the page code (ergostat/web/, ergostat/web/static/) or its demo (examples/<demo>/). Walking all 46 at a $2 session costs $92, more than the $40 daily cap (dev/model/budget.yaml). Nothing today says when a story is stale. The filed reruns fix the walk to milestones by hand.

Change: add `stories.py due`, a program block every 15 minutes in dev/model/design.yaml. For each story not due and not retired, it compares its walked_sha with main. When `git diff --name-only walked_sha..main` touches ergostat/web/** or examples/<the story's demo>/**, the story is stale. A story never walked is stale. Stale stories are made due (story.due, with why: the files and the merge) in this order: impossible first, then possible, not-yet, obvious, then the oldest walk. At most [design] due_per_day (default 4, held to 0..46) are made due per local day, counted from the record. `stories.py due --all` makes every story due once, ignoring the cap, for the coordinator's first sweep. A main that cannot be read stops it with nothing made due. In the model: a flow stories-made-due, and the goal stories-walked (stories-due <= 0).

Definition of done:
1. A merge that touches ergostat/web/static/items.js makes stale stories due, failing first, up to the cap.
2. A merge touching only docs/ makes none due.
3. A merge touching examples/the-job/ makes only the-job's stories due.
4. The day's cap holds across runs, and --all ignores it once.
5. An unreadable git state makes nothing due and exits non-zero.
6. factory.toml documents [design] due_per_day.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-designer-walks-stories
gaps.title: The designer queue: a session per due story starts its demo, walks it in a browser as a newcomer, and records a verdict with screenshots
gaps.definition:
Problem: once stories are items, nothing walks them. The walks so far were done by hand by design reviewers outside the factory (the design folder's story-results, 8 group files). The filed reruns ask an implementor to write a results file, so the verdicts never reach the model, no stock moves and no goal is off. The owner wants designers to own the stories and re-test them after UI merges.

Change: add a block `designer` (type ai, system design, pool 1, lease 60m, timeout 1h) in dev/model/design.yaml. It takes {kind: story, at: due, to: [obvious, possible, impossible, not-yet]}, and is driven by an expr designer-when = goal.stories-walked.off * (1 - goal.ai-budget.off).
- dev/bin/design.py (new) clones main read-only (agents.clone, at origin/main) and writes a brief from dev/prompts/designer.md (new). The brief holds the story's text, its demo and URL, the newcomer rules of the stories file's "How to test a story", the owner's design decisions (the knowledge block's decisions), and the commands to start the demo (demo_up.py) and walk it (walk.py --shots /shots).
- It runs one designer session.
- It parses <walk verdict="obvious|possible|impossible|not-yet"> steps taken, what was seen, why </walk>.
- It copies /shots to run/stories/<story>-<n>/ and says story.<verdict> with walked_at, walked_sha (the clone's), steps, why, screenshots (paths), and cost.
- A session with no <walk>, or an unknown verdict, is a failed attempt (the lease retries once). It is never recorded as a verdict.
- The prompt tells the session it is a newcomer who has not read the docs, to stop at the story's own bound, to judge from the screenshots it reads back, and never to edit anything.

Definition of done:
1. A due story with the stand-in designer saying a verdict moves to that state, with walked_sha, steps and the screenshots copied under run/stories/.
2. A missing or unknown verdict leaves it due, with the attempt failed and the reason recorded.
3. The block waits while the day's budget is spent.
4. The story's item page lists its screenshots and verdict history (fields only, no new UI).
5. The model loads and the flow stories-walked is driven by the block.
6. dev/README.md "The story queue" says how a walk runs.

gaps.name: research-design-queues-walk-findings-as-gaps
gaps.title: A walk that is not possible and obvious files its findings as small gaps, linked to the story, which is due again when they merge
gaps.definition:
Problem: a verdict alone fixes nothing. In the design review, each failed story's findings were turned into gaps by hand (the owner's list, the filed redesign gaps). The owner wants the designer queue to file findings as gaps. That needs bounds: a 46-story sweep could otherwise flood the gap queue (lesson-4, review-lessons.md). Duplicates must be refused: the same finding on the next walk must not file again. When a gap filed for a story merges, the story should be walked again rather than wait for an unrelated UI merge.

Change: the designer prompt asks for, under a non-obvious verdict, up to 3 <finding step="N" screenshot="name.png">what failed, in one or two sentences</finding> tags, outside code fences.
- design.py requests each finding as a gap: gap/story-<code>-<hash8 of the story and normalised finding>. Its title is "<code>: <finding, cut>". The fields are source: story, size: S (plan-by-size: no planner session), story, the screenshot path, and a definition written by the program to run/defs/<branch>.md in the house shape: Problem (the finding, the story's done-when, the screenshot path), Change ("make this step possible and obvious within the owner's decisions"), Definition of done (the story's done-when for this step), Files (left to the implementor), Acceptance ("the story walked again passes this step"), and a budget of 80 lines.
- At most 3 per walk and [design] gaps_per_day (default 6) per day, counted from the record. An id that exists in any state is never requested again.
- Each filed gap is added to the story's gaps.
- `stories.py due` also makes a story due when one of its gaps merges, ahead of the cap's ordering, still within the cap.

Definition of done:
1. An impossible walk with two findings requests two S gaps, each with a run/defs definition naming the story and the screenshot, linked on the story.
2. The same finding on the next walk requests nothing.
3. Five findings in one walk request 3, and the rest are noted on the story as not filed (cap).
4. The daily cap holds across walks.
5. A finding inside a code fence or tool output is ignored.
6. A merged linked gap makes the story due.
7. dev/README.md says so.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-remote-parts-are-data
gaps.title: A remote's parts are data here: never integrated, fitted or judged unexercised locally
gaps.definition:
Problem: remote-systems.md §6 and SPEC §4c say a remote's stocks are endogenous there and exogenous here: read as data series, never integrated; the local residuals, coherence and 'not exercised by the record' leave its parts out. On main the served flows keep their equations (ergostat/remote/serve.py:26, 'equation' in PART_KEEP['flows']), compose drops one only when it names a part left out (ergostat/remote/compose.py:440), and ergostat/numbers/simulate.py:96 integrates every stock with flows, so a remote's stock is integrated in the local replay and the projection (open and closed loop), and ergostat/numbers/fit.py:211-217 puts it in the local fit total that the modelling goals hold. ergostat/numbers/exercised.py:56-117 judges remote parts 'never-moved'/'no-variation'. ergostat/remote/__init__.py:18-21 claims the exclusion, but only state.py:193 and :623 apply it.
Change: one helper decides what is a remote's (remote_parts, already there); simulate.plan leaves remote stocks out of what it integrates by default (taken as measured, like `given`), and the projection carries them as inputs (held or trended, as any input); the fit total, the residual examination and the exercised findings skip remote parts. The remote's flow equations stay as they are: the equation finder and the estimate still use them for texts written for the remote's owner (numbers/remote_text.py), which must keep working.
Definition of done:
1. simulate.plan(spec) with integrate=None integrates no stock in remote_parts(spec); each is 'given' in Run.how and a note says 'stock.X is remote NAME's: taken as read, never integrated here'. An explicit integrate= set is honoured as given (callers that ask still get it).
2. simulate.project and closedloop.closed carry a remote stock as an input (inputs='hold' or 'trend', as every other input), never as integrated state; a local flow from or to a remote stock still moves the local stock.
3. fit.compare leaves remote stocks out of 'stocks', 'accounting' and 'total' and lists them under a new key 'remote' (ref -> remote name), so the local model-error goal is not moved by a remote's dynamics.
4. residuals (examinable/unread) and exercised.quiet/findings skip remote parts.
5. Texts for a remote's owner (remote_text) are made exactly as before: tests/test_remote_proposals.py passes unchanged.
6. SPEC §4c says this in one paragraph (what is given, what is left out, what still uses the remote's equations); GAPS's remote entry says it is done.
Files: ergostat/numbers/simulate.py, ergostat/numbers/fit.py, ergostat/numbers/residuals.py, ergostat/numbers/exercised.py, ergostat/remote/__init__.py (docstring), docs/SPEC.md, docs/GAPS.md, tests/test_remote_analysis.py (new).
Acceptance tests (tests/test_remote_analysis.py, a local model composing a planted remote cache as tests/test_remote_chain.py does, with recorded readings): test_remote_stock_is_given_not_integrated (Run.how is 'given' and the replayed value equals the readings; fails if plan integrates it); test_projection_carries_remote_stock_as_input (hold: flat at its last reading; a local flow drained from it still moves the local stock); test_fit_total_leaves_remote_out (a remote stock whose readings the remote equation fits badly leaves the local total unchanged and is listed under 'remote'); test_exercised_skips_remote (a flat remote stock gives no never-moved finding; a flat local one still does); the existing remote proposals tests pass.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-explain-remote-parts
gaps.title: explain names a remote's parts and the loops that cross into a remote
gaps.definition:
Problem: remote-systems.md §6: 'Loops are found through remote parts ... explain names the remote parts on it'. ergostat/spec/explain.py:141-157 (feedback) lists every loop with no remote marking, and neither a part's nor a system's explanation (explain.py:389, :495) says a part is a remote's, where it runs or how old its readings are, although docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md §3a tells agents to use `ergostat explain system.incidents` to look before referencing. remote_of (ergostat/remote/__init__.py:9) and box (:61) already know it.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-mcp-remotes-tool
gaps.title: Agents see the model's remotes through an MCP tool
gaps.definition:
Problem: an agent modelling a system that composes a remote must know which parts are the remote's (it may not edit them; a proposal for them becomes text), whether the remote answers, and the texts waiting for its owner. All of this is only in the CLI (ergostat/cli/remote.py:17-23: status, events, proposals); ergostat/mcp.py:30-191 has no remote tool. The owner's rule is that features go to agent tools and skills, not CLIs.
Change: one read-only MCP tool, `remotes`, built on the same functions the CLI uses (no new reads of the remote; no refresh is triggered).
Definition of done:
1. `remotes` with no argument returns, per remote: name, url, version, read (seconds ago), state (ok, unreachable, unknown, as remote.box), why when failing, part count by kind, missing references (remote-reference-unresolved), and its box's show.
2. `remotes` with `name` adds the list of its parts (local name -> remote name, kind) up to 500, and `proposals: true` adds the open texts for its owner as `ergostat remote proposals NAME --json` gives them.
3. A name that is not a key of remotes: is an error naming the model's remotes. A model with none answers {remotes: []}.
4. It works on the last good model when the YAML is broken, as `remote proposals` does (goodmodel.READ_WHAT), and writes nothing.
5. The MCP tool list's description and AGENT-GUIDE §3a say when to call it (before referencing a remote's part, and before proposing a change near one).
