gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-remote-stale-finding
gaps.title: check and the Check page say remote-stale when a remote's readings fail
gaps.definition:
Problem: remote-systems.md §5 says stale or failing readings give 'remote-unreachable and remote-stale findings' on the Check page and in `check`. Only remote-unreachable exists, raised when the model fetch fails (ergostat/remote/compose.py:180-188). When the model answers but its readings fail or are refused as stale (ergostat/remote/readings.py:198-204; status read_ok False, ergostat/remote/cache.py:108-116) only the status's attention says so (ergostat/remote/__init__.py:40); `check` is silent.
Change: compose adds a `remote-stale` finding from the same status the box reads.
Definition of done:
1. When a remote's status has read_ok False (and its model did answer), compose adds a finding `remote-stale` on system.NAME: 'remote NAME: its readings fail (WHY) since T; its measures here are N old'. With read_ok True or never read, none.
2. remote-unreachable and remote-stale are never both given for one remote at one load: unreachable wins.
3. SPEC §4c lists remote-stale with the other finding codes; AGENT-GUIDE §3a step 4 says what to do (the remote answers but its sensors there are not reading: tell its owner).
Files: ergostat/remote/compose.py, docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, tests/test_remote.py.
Acceptance tests: test_remote_stale_finding (status planted with read_ok False: check gives remote-stale; set True: gone); test_unreachable_wins_over_stale.
Size budget: 50 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-template-exports
gaps.title: A template declares its exports; a reference to its internals is a finding
gaps.definition:
Problem: docs/proposals/external-systems.md (Deployment) says a shared module's ports are its public interface (`exports:`): internals change freely, and removing or renaming a port is a breaking change. Today any part of an instance can be named by its full name from anywhere (docs/SPEC.md:142), so a library author cannot change any internal part without breaking someone, and nothing tells a user which parts are meant to be read. Template files take only HEAD keys (ergostat/library/templates.py:24) and have no `exports`.
Change: an optional template key `exports:`, a list of the template's own refs (`stock.unanswered`, `goal.answered-in-time`, `flow.x`, `auxiliary.y`, `block.z`). Absent means all parts are exported (no change for existing templates).
Definition of done:
1. templates.read accepts `exports`; each entry must be a ref to a part the template defines (after each:/if: expansion is not needed: names written in the template's sections), else bad-template naming the entry. For an untrusted template each entry must also match the SAFE name rule.
2. After expansion, a reference from outside an instance (the owner's parts or another instance's) to a part of the instance that is not exported is a finding `template-internal-reference` at the referencing line: 'NAME is internal to instance I (template T exports: ...)'. A reference inside the instance, or an instance within it, is never a finding. Inner instances' exports count for references from outside the outer instance only if the outer re-exports them (`exports` may name an inner instance's exported ref by the inner's full template-local name).
3. The `templates` MCP tool and `author.library` show `exports` (marked as library text for an untrusted template, like the other fields).
4. One built-in template (respond-to) declares exports, with its README line, and every built-in demo still checks clean.
5. SPEC §2a documents exports and the finding; AGENT-GUIDE says to reference only exports and to write exports when writing a template.
Files: ergostat/library/templates.py, ergostat/library/uses.py (record each instance's exports in doc.uses), ergostat/spec/compile.py (the reference check), ergostat/library/author.py, ergostat/library/templates/respond-to.yaml, docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, tests/test_template_exports.py (new).
Acceptance tests: test_exports_must_name_own_parts (an unknown ref is bad-template); test_reference_to_internal_part_is_finding (owner goal on a non-exported stock: finding at the goal's line; on an exported one: none); test_reference_within_instance_free; test_no_exports_means_all; test_templates_tool_shows_exports; scripts/demo_check.py passes for every demo.
Size budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-fetched-untrusted-held
gaps.title: A fetched library not marked trusted is held by the untrusted gate, not refused outright
gaps.definition:
Problem: library-fetch's definition makes every use of a fetched library without `trust: owner` the error library-untrusted, 'found and listed, but never expanded', and says 'the trust gate by provenance and the sandbox are later gaps that will relax this'. That gate is on main for untrusted folders: Template.trust drives it (ergostat/library/templates.py:59-64, :87-89), uses.one/plan hold a chain from the first untrusted template down (ergostat/library/uses.py:57-76, :122-125), bounds and marks follow, and library-sandbox-sensors/-blocks run its programs sandboxed. So a fetched library from a colleague is unusable unless the owner trusts it whole, which is the riskier choice.
Change: a fetched library without trust: owner reads its templates with trust 'untrusted', exactly as a `{folder: PATH}` library entry, and the blanket refusal is removed.
Definition of done:
1. Templates from a fetched library with no `trust: owner` have trust 'untrusted'; with it, 'owner'. Nothing else sets trust for them.
2. They are looked up after every trusted template (never shadow one, as find_all does for untrusted folders) and the shadowing note says the library's name, marked as library text.
3. A use of one is held: the allowlist (trust.py), R3 text rule, bounds (bounds.py), marks and untrusted-limit apply unchanged; a refusal is library-untrusted or untrusted-text at the owner's use: line, naming the library (name, commit) rather than a folder path.
4. library-fetch's tests that asserted the blanket refusal are changed to assert the held behaviour: structure-only uses compile, a use that makes a command is refused.
5. SPEC §2a and SECURITY 'Libraries you did not write' say fetched libraries are trusted the same way as folders; GAPS updated.
Files: ergostat/library/fetched.py, ergostat/library/templates.py, ergostat/library/uses.py, tests/test_library_fetch.py, tests/test_library_trust.py, docs/SPEC.md, docs/SECURITY.md, docs/GAPS.md.
Acceptance tests: test_fetched_untrusted_structure_compiles (a file:// library offering a structure-only template, no trust: used and compiled, its instance marked untrusted); test_fetched_untrusted_command_refused (a template with a run: is refused as library-untrusted naming the library); test_fetched_untrusted_never_shadows (a trusted folder's template of the same name wins); test_fetched_trusted_unchanged.
Size budget: 80 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-qualified-use
gaps.title: use: LIBRARY/TEMPLATE names which library a template comes from
gaps.definition:
Problem: library-fetch looks templates up by bare name in order (the owner's folders, then fetched libraries in config order, then ergostat's) and notes shadowing. With two libraries offering a template of one name (both teams' keep-under), only the first can be used, and a use does not say where its template comes from, so a reader of ergostat.yaml cannot tell, and adding a library can silently change which template an existing use gets. The parked libraries branch planned `use: NAME/TEMPLATE` (docs/roadmap/overnight/libraries.md on origin/libraries).
Change: `use:` takes `LIB/TEMPLATE` for a fetched library's template; a bare name works as today.
Definition of done:
1. `use: LIB/TEMPLATE` resolves only in fetched library LIB (a key of libraries:); LIB unknown or not loaded is unknown-template naming the libraries and, when LIB was refused, its refusal reason. TEMPLATE not offered by LIB is unknown-template listing what LIB offers.
2. A bare name that two or more sources offer is still resolved as today, and check adds a finding `template-ambiguous` naming each source and suggesting the qualified form.
3. Nested uses inside a library's template may use `LIB/TEMPLATE` too; a bare name inside a library's template resolves first in its own library.
4. The `templates` MCP tool lists each fetched template under its qualified name, and add_use writes the qualified name for one.
5. Instance naming is unchanged (the instance's key names its parts); where.template records the qualified name.
6. SPEC §2a and AGENT-GUIDE document it.
Files: ergostat/library/uses.py, ergostat/library/templates.py (lookup), ergostat/library/author.py, ergostat/mcp.py (add_use), docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, tests/test_library_fetch.py or tests/test_library_qualified.py (new).
Acceptance tests: test_qualified_use_picks_library (two file:// libraries offering keep-under: each qualified use expands its own); test_bare_name_ambiguous_finding; test_unknown_library_or_template_said; test_inner_bare_name_resolves_in_own_library; test_add_use_writes_qualified_name.
Size budget: 100 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-libraries-listed
gaps.title: check and the templates tool say each library: where from, pin, trust, and whether its programs run
gaps.definition:
Problem: after library-fetch a model can depend on several git libraries, but nothing lists them: check says only errors (library-unlocked, library-altered, ...), and the templates tool's entries carry `from` and `trust` (ergostat/library/author.py:39-50; templates.py:66-68) without the library's name, url, version or pinned commit. The parked branch's done-when asked that 'check prints a line for every library: where it comes from, its version and commit, the scripts it brings, and whether they will run'; nobody can review what a model trusts without it.
Change: one function describes each library from what load already read (no network, no git).
Definition of done:
1. ergostat/library/fetched.py gives, per libraries: entry: name, git url, version, path, commit (12 hex), tree ok or the refusal code and reason, trust (owner | untrusted), templates offered, and per template whether its programs would run on the owner's shell, in the sandbox, or are refused (from the trust gate's verdict, failing closed: anything not proven owner is said 'sandbox or refused').
2. `ergostat check` prints one note per library (`library NAME: URL @ VERSION (commit C), trust T, N templates; programs: ...`), code `library`, never an error; nothing for a model with no libraries:.
3. The templates MCP tool's entries for a fetched template carry `library: {name, version, commit}`; library text stays marked for untrusted ones.
4. `ergostat library` with no subcommand prints the same listing offline (as the old plan's 'list'), on the last good model when the YAML is broken, writing nothing.
5. SPEC §2a documents the listing.
Files: ergostat/library/fetched.py, ergostat/cli/library.py, ergostat/cli/spec_cmds.py (check's notes), ergostat/library/author.py, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_library_fetch.py.
Acceptance tests: test_check_lists_each_library (two fetched libraries, one trusted: two notes with commit and trust); test_listing_says_refused_library (a library-altered one is listed with its reason); test_templates_tool_carries_library_pin; test_library_listing_offline (no git process run: the runner monkeypatched to fail).
Size budget: 110 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-library-update-check
gaps.title: An update to a library is reviewed before it is taken: what the new version breaks and changes
gaps.definition:
Problem: docs/proposals/external-systems.md (Deployment): 'Updating a pinned version is a reviewable change: ergostat check against the new version lists what broke, which numbers you depend on moved'. library-fetch's `fetch --update` resolves and swaps in the new commit at once; the first sign of trouble is a broken model after the swap. Nobody, agent or owner, can see an update's effect before taking it, and nothing says a newer version exists.
Change: a dry run that fetches the candidate into fetch's temporary folder (same allowlists, caps, timeouts and flock), never swaps it or writes the lock, compiles the model twice in memory (the locked copy and the candidate) and reports the difference.
Definition of done:
1. `ergostat library fetch NAME --update --dry-run` and an MCP tool `library_update` (name, optional version) do the same: resolve the entry's version (or the one given, checked by library-fetch's ref allowlist), fetch into a mkdtemp folder under .libraries, and remove it afterwards whatever happens; .libraries/NAME and libraries.lock are unchanged (asserted by hash in the test).
2. The report: commit from -> to, and the tags pointing at commits newer than the pinned one when the remote lists them (one `git ls-remote --tags` under library-fetch's git environment, refused schemes and refs as fetch refuses them); templates added and removed; per use of the library: parameters added, removed, newly required, defaults changed, exports removed (when template-exports has landed, else omitted); parts the instance makes added and removed by full name; parameter values that moved (name, from, to); errors and findings the candidate model has that the current one does not (a broken reference first).
3. Exit 0 when the candidate compiles with no new error, 1 otherwise; the MCP answer says the same as `ok`.
4. Nothing of the candidate reaches the running model, the good-model snapshot or the record.
5. SPEC §2a, AGENT-GUIDE ('before taking an update, run library_update and show the owner what breaks'), GAPS.
Files: ergostat/library/compare.py (new: the two compiles and the diff), ergostat/library/fetch.py (fetch into a folder without swapping), ergostat/cli/library.py, ergostat/mcp.py, docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, docs/GAPS.md, tests/test_library_update.py (new; file:// repositories built in tmp_path).
Acceptance tests: test_dry_run_changes_nothing (copy and lock hashes equal before and after; no .tmp- folder left); test_report_lists_removed_param_and_part (upstream removes a parameter and a stock the owner references: both listed, the broken reference first, exit 1); test_report_lists_moved_value; test_report_names_newer_tags; test_bad_version_refused_without_git; test_mcp_library_update_matches_cli.
Size budget: 260 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-known-controller-laws
gaps.title: An external block may declare a known law (kubernetes-hpa, alert-rule), checked and drawn
gaps.definition:
Problem: docs/proposals/external-systems.md: an observed controller's 'law is declared where it is known. The HPA's is public ... A library of known controllers ships with ergostat'. GAPS (Identifying existing controllers, Left) lists 'the library of known laws (law: kubernetes-hpa, declared and tested against the record)'. Today an external block takes only `agent` and `identify` (ergostat/spec/compile.py:94, :1466-1473); its law can only be identified (ergostat/numbers/extlaw.py, families onoff, proportional, pi, stepper at :24), and the HPA's multiplicative rule is in none of them.
Change: a catalogue of known laws and a `law:` key on an external block that has `identify:` (which says what it reads and sets).
Definition of done:
1. ergostat/control/laws.py: a catalogue, each law with its parameters (type, default, required, bounds) and a constructor of an extlaw.Law. kubernetes-hpa: target (number > 0, required), min (integer >= 0, default 1), max (integer, required, >= min), tolerance (default 0.1), stabilize-down (duration, default 5m), stabilize-up (duration, default 0s), every (duration, default 15s). alert-rule: threshold (required), side (above | below, default above), for (duration, default 0s), as the onoff family with levels 0 and 1.
2. extlaw gains the `ratio` family's step (desired = ceil(u * x / target) when |x / target - 1| > tolerance, else u; a scale-down takes the largest desired over the stabilize-down window; clamped to [min, max]), used by run/step like every family. No fitting of it here.
3. compile: `law: {kind: NAME, ...params}` on an external block; an unknown kind, an unknown or ill-typed parameter, a missing required one, or `law:` without `identify:` is an error at that key (bad-law), naming the catalogue's kinds or the law's parameters.
4. Blocks draws a declared law in the block as its function (short form, e.g. 'u = clamp(ceil(u·y/0.6), 3, 40)', marked 'declared kubernetes-hpa'), taking the place of 'identified' when both exist and saying the identified one in its rows; explain says the declared law in words.
5. SPEC §12d and AGENT-GUIDE document `law:` and the catalogue.
Files: ergostat/control/laws.py (new), ergostat/numbers/extlaw.py, ergostat/spec/compile.py, ergostat/spec/ir.py (Block param), ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/spec/explain.py, docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, tests/test_known_laws.py (new).
Acceptance tests: test_hpa_law_compiles_and_draws (a model with an external block law kubernetes-hpa: the Blocks answer's fn says declared and its short form); test_bad_law_refused (unknown kind, unknown param, max < min, law without identify: each bad-law at its key); test_ratio_step_matches_hpa_rule (scale up immediately, scale down only after the window, tolerance band holds, clamps); test_alert_rule_is_onoff.
Size budget: 220 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-declared-law-tested
gaps.title: A declared law is tested against the record: does the controller behave as configured
gaps.definition:
Problem: external-systems.md: 'where it is declared, the declaration is tested against what the controller actually did: the fit says whether it behaves as configured'. After known-controller-laws a declared law is drawn but never compared with the record; identification (ergostat/numbers/external.py:59-74, extlaw.judge at extlaw.py:349) runs only on its own fitted laws.
Change: run the declared law on the record's measured input with extlaw.run, and judge it with the identification's measures on the same held-out quarter.
Definition of done:
1. external.declared(p, spec, name, since, until) returns the declared Law judged on the record (skill one step ahead, R² run free, points), using the same grid as identify, or why not (too little record, as identify says).
2. A finding `external-law-disagrees` when the declared law's held-out skill is below 0 or the identified law's held-out error is lower by the parsimony rule's margin (the identification's own scoring): 'block B: declared kubernetes-hpa (short) fits its record worse than ...: it does not behave as configured', with the points and the window. `external-law-holds` is never a finding; the loop's panel table shows held-out fit for the declared law beside the identified one.
3. /api/loop-control for a goal whose loop holds the block includes `declared: {kind, short, skill, r2, points}`.
4. With no `law:` nothing changes (the identify tests pass unchanged).
5. SPEC §12d documents the test and its finding, with the claim limited to 'fits the record worse', not 'misconfigured'.
Files: ergostat/numbers/external.py, ergostat/web (the loop-control answer's module), docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_known_laws.py.
Acceptance tests: test_declared_law_that_matches_holds (a synthetic HPA record made by the declared law: no finding, skill > 0.5); test_declared_law_with_wrong_target_disagrees (the record made with target 0.5, declared 0.8: external-law-disagrees naming the window); test_too_little_record_says_why; test_loop_control_carries_declared.
Size budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-declared-law-projected
gaps.title: A declared law runs in the closed-loop projection and its risk
gaps.definition:
Problem: the closed-loop projection runs an external block only as its identified law (ergostat/numbers/external.py:155-171 models(); closedloop.py:14, :431 'identified model'). A declared law (known-controller-laws) is the owner's statement of what the controller does and is all there is when the record is too short to identify one, but the projection ignores it, so a what-if on an HPA's target cannot be projected.
Change: external.models prefers a declared law, else the identified one.
Definition of done:
1. For an external block with `law:`, models() returns an ExternalModel with form 'declared', basis 'its declaration', the declared Law, started from the record as settle() starts an identified one; with no law the identified path is unchanged.
2. The projection's notes and Run.how say 'declared law' for its flow, and the risk samples none of a declared law's numbers (they are stated, not estimated).
3. A what-if may change a declared law's parameter (`block.B.target=0.5` in parse_whatif's form) and the projection runs with it; an unknown parameter is refused naming the law's parameters.
4. external-not-run applies to a declared law as to an identified one.
5. SPEC §12c and §12d say it.
Files: ergostat/numbers/external.py, ergostat/numbers/closedloop.py, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_known_laws.py.
Acceptance tests: test_projection_runs_declared_law (a short record with no identifiable law: replicas projected by the HPA rule under rising load reach the ceiling at max); test_declared_wins_over_identified (both present: how says declared); test_whatif_changes_declared_target (lower target: more replicas projected); test_no_law_unchanged.
Size budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-hpa-ratio-family
gaps.title: Identification fits the HPA's multiplicative rule as its own family
gaps.definition:
Problem: GAPS (Identifying existing controllers, Left): 'the HPA's multiplicative rule as its own family'. extlaw's families (ergostat/numbers/extlaw.py:24) approximate an autoscaler with the stepper (fixed steps up and down), which mistells an HPA whose step grows with the load: desired = ceil(current × metric / target). known-controller-laws adds the ratio family's step but not its fit, so an undeclared HPA is never identified as one.
Change: extlaw.fit tries `ratio` beside the others, fitting target, tolerance, the stabilisation window, min and max from the record, chosen by the same held-out score and parsimony rule.
Definition of done:
1. _fit_ratio(xs, us, dt): target by least squares on the moves (log u_next/u = log x/target over moves), tolerance from the largest |x/target − 1| with no move, stabilize-down from the shortest time from a lower desired to the move down, min and max from the record's bounds when it saturates; None with too few moves (MIN_MOVES).
2. FAMILIES includes 'ratio'; Law.said and short describe it ('u ← ceil(u·x/0.6), within [3, 40], down after 5m'); its standard errors are the target's and tolerance's.
3. On a stepper-made record the stepper still wins; on an HPA-made record ratio wins (asserted over seeds, with the rate stated in the report).
4. Blocks draws an identified ratio law as it draws a declared one, marked identified.
5. SPEC §12d's table of families gains the row.
Files: ergostat/numbers/extlaw.py, ergostat/blockdiagram.py (sketch), docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_identify_ratio.py (new).
Acceptance tests: test_ratio_identified_on_hpa_record (20 seeds of a synthetic HPA with noise: ratio chosen in at least 18, target within 10%); test_stepper_still_wins_on_stepper_record (20 seeds, at least 18); test_ratio_needs_moves (too few: why says so).
Size budget: 140 net lines.

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-autoscaler-template
gaps.title: Built-in templates for known controllers: an observed autoscaler and an alert rule
gaps.definition:
Problem: external-systems.md: 'A library of known controllers ships with ergostat as model fragments with their equations and parameters ... You include one and bind it to your metrics.' The built-in library (ergostat/library/templates/, SPEC §2a 'The built-in library') has respond-to, re-ping, steps, keep-under and others, but no fragment for a controller ergostat observes, so every user writes the replicas stock, the utilisation auxiliary, the external block and its identify: by hand.
Change: two built-in templates using the declared laws.
Definition of done:
1. `observed-autoscaler`: parameters target, min, max (and the HPA's optional ones), replicas (a sensor query or command, with a stand-in that creeps with a made-up load), load (likewise), within, description. It makes: stock replicas with its sensor, auxiliary utilisation (= load / replicas, or measured when a utilisation query is given), a goal on utilisation at the target, an external block reading utilisation and setting replicas with law kubernetes-hpa and identify; `reading:` says it in control (an observed controller, a stepper of replicas holding utilisation, r/y/u) and system dynamics (replicas a stock, scaling its flows).
2. `alert-rule`: threshold, side, for, the signal (a query), what it pages (an item kind or nothing); an external block with law alert-rule, the signal auxiliary, and a stock of firing alerts.
3. Both compile on stand-ins alone (template-stand-in finding, as other templates), run offline, and draw in both views; their Blocks loop shows r (target), y (utilisation), u (replicas).
4. The templates tool lists them; docs/ADDING.md and `ergostat help adding` describe them; SPEC's built-in list names them.
Files: ergostat/library/templates/observed-autoscaler.yaml, ergostat/library/templates/alert-rule.yaml, docs/ADDING.md, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_templates.py.
Acceptance tests: test_observed_autoscaler_on_stand_ins (compiles, one external block with law kubernetes-hpa, the goal on utilisation, template-stand-in listed); test_observed_autoscaler_blocks_loop (Blocks answer: r, y, u named as above); test_alert_rule_template_compiles; existing template tests pass.
Size budget: 130 net lines (YAML counted).

gaps.name: remote-and-libraries-shared-library-demo
gaps.title: A worked shared library: two models using one library, and a guide to writing one
gaps.definition:
Problem: there is a worked remote (examples/remote-pair/) but no worked shared library: no example shows a library used by two projects, one trusting it and one not, and docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md (lines 366-383) says only how to read an untrusted library's refusals, not how to write a library for others (layout, parameters, stand-ins, exports, scripts under ${here}, tagging a version for fetch). The parked branch's examples/library-demo/ was never merged.
Change: an example and a guide section.
Definition of done:
1. examples/shared-library/: a library folder `library/` (two templates, one with a sensor script under ${here} and exports, one structure-only), and two models: `team-a/` lists it as an owner folder (its script runs on the owner's shell), `team-b/` lists it as `{folder: ...}` untrusted (its structure template is used; the scripted one's sensor runs sandboxed when the OS sandbox is there, else its reading fails 'no OS sandbox here', as library-sandbox-sensors says). README says what each shows and how the same folder becomes a git library with libraries: (pointing at the fetch docs).
2. scripts/demo_check.py passes both models; team-b's check shows the untrusted marks and no untrusted-limit error.
3. AGENT-GUIDE gains 'Writing a library for others': folder layout, a template per file, parameters with stand-ins, exports (template-exports), scripts under ${here} and that an untrusted user's run is sandboxed, version tags for fetch, and never asking users to mark it trusted.
4. examples/README.md lists it.
Files: examples/shared-library/ (library/, team-a/, team-b/, README.md), examples/README.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, tests/test_demo_check.py (or tests/test_shared_library_demo.py).
Acceptance tests: test_shared_library_demo_checks (both models compile clean); test_team_b_sensor_sandboxed (the sensor's reads says ', sandboxed'; a reading where the sandbox exists records a value, else fails with the no-sandbox reason and records nothing); test_team_b_internal_reference_finding (a planted reference to a non-exported part gives template-internal-reference).
Size budget: 200 net lines (YAML, scripts and README counted; tests not).
